triage.name: Abdominal Pain
triage.reason: A symptom, not a diagnosis; students can't reach a single diagnosis from it, though specific causes of abdominal pain make good cases.

triage.name: Abscess
triage.reason: A pathologic finding rather than a specific diagnosis; presentation and workup vary entirely by site, so it is too broad for a single case.

triage.name: Acne
triage.reason: Common dermatologic diagnosis reachable by history and skin exam, with recognizable lesion types and clear management decisions.

triage.name: Acoustic Neuroma
triage.reason: Unilateral hearing loss and tinnitus with a clear diagnostic pathway through audiometry and imaging; good for teaching cranial nerve and posterior fossa localization.

triage.name: Acute Bronchitis
triage.reason: Very common cough illness where the key skill is distinguishing it from pneumonia and avoiding unnecessary antibiotics; reachable by history and exam.

triage.name: Acute Lymphocytic Leukemia
triage.reason: Serious hematologic malignancy with a distinctive presentation of cytopenias, lymphadenopathy and organomegaly; workup via CBC and smear is teachable.

triage.name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
triage.reason: Presents with fatigue, bleeding, and infection; diagnosis reachable via CBC with blasts and marrow biopsy, with important look-alikes.

triage.name: Addison Disease
triage.reason: Chronic fatigue, weight loss, hyperpigmentation and salt craving lead to a clear diagnosis via cortisol and ACTH testing.

triage.name: Adhesions
triage.reason: A pathologic process rather than a diagnosis reached by interview; presents nonspecifically as obstruction or pain, better captured by those conditions.

triage.name: Adrenal Gland Cancer
triage.reason: Adrenal mass or hormone excess presents with hypertension, weight change, or incidental imaging finding; workup is well defined.

triage.name: Adrenal Gland Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category covering many distinct adrenal diseases; not a single diagnosis a student can reach.

triage.name: After Surgery
triage.reason: A care state, not a diagnosis; postoperative complications are better modeled as specific conditions.

triage.name: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD)
triage.reason: Diagnosis made by history of impaired control, craving, tolerance and withdrawal; common and high-yield for interview skills.

triage.name: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) Treatment
triage.reason: A treatment topic rather than a diagnosis; management is not reached by interview and workup alone.

triage.name: Allergy
triage.reason: A broad immune mechanism, not a specific diagnosis; specific allergic conditions are better case topics.

triage.name: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency
triage.reason: Early emphysema or liver disease with family history leads to a specific diagnosis via serum AAT level and genotype.

triage.name: Alzheimer's Caregivers
triage.reason: A caregiving role, not a patient diagnosis; no clinical presentation to interview or examine.

triage.name: Alzheimer's Disease
triage.reason: Progressive memory loss and functional decline diagnosed clinically with cognitive testing and reversible-cause workup.

triage.name: Amblyopia
triage.reason: Reduced vision in one eye found on pediatric vision screening; diagnosis by acuity and refractive testing.

triage.name: Amino Acid Metabolism Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of many distinct inherited disorders; not a single diagnosis.

triage.name: Amyloidosis
triage.reason: Multisystem findings such as nephrotic proteinuria, heart failure and neuropathy lead to biopsy-proven diagnosis.

triage.name: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
triage.reason: Progressive weakness with upper and lower motor neuron signs; diagnosis by history, exam and electrodiagnostic testing.

triage.name: Anal Cancer
triage.reason: Bleeding or anal mass with risk factors; diagnosis by exam and biopsy, with staging workup.

triage.name: Anal Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of distinct anorectal conditions; not a single diagnosis.

triage.name: Anaphylaxis
triage.reason: Acute allergic emergency recognized by history and exam; rapid recognition and treatment are essential.

triage.name: Anemia
triage.reason: A laboratory finding rather than a specific diagnosis; specific anemias are better case topics.

triage.name: Aneurysms
triage.reason: A patient with a pulsatile mass, pain, or rupture can be worked up to a specific aneurysm diagnosis, though the term itself is broad and cases usually specify location.

triage.name: Angina
triage.reason: Chest pain is a classic undifferentiated symptom case; history, ECG, and troponin lead to stable angina versus ACS and its mimics.

triage.name: Animal Bites
triage.reason: A bite wound is a concrete presentation requiring history of the animal, exam for tendon/nerve/joint involvement, and decisions on antibiotics, rabies and tetanus.

triage.name: Animal Diseases and Your Health
triage.reason: A broad public-health category of zoonoses, not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interviewing and examining one patient.

triage.name: Ankle Injuries and Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of ankle harm rather than one diagnosis; specific entities like ankle fracture or sprain are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Ankylosing Spondylitis
triage.reason: Young adult with chronic inflammatory back pain and stiffness; history, exam, inflammatory markers and sacroiliac imaging lead to the diagnosis.

triage.name: Anthrax
triage.reason: A defined infectious disease with characteristic skin, inhalational or GI presentations that can be reached from exposure history and exam, though rare in the US.

triage.name: Anxiety
triage.reason: A common psychiatric presentation with somatic complaints; diagnosis is reached by history and ruling out mimics, and it teaches interview skills.

triage.name: Aortic Aneurysm
triage.reason: Often asymptomatic or presenting with back/abdominal pain or rupture; exam, ultrasound or CT lead to a specific diagnosis with high-stakes management.

triage.name: Aphasia
triage.reason: A language deficit that can be characterized by bedside interview and exam, with localization and stroke workup leading to the diagnosis.

triage.name: Aplastic Anemia
triage.reason: Pancytopenia with fatigue, bleeding and infection; CBC, smear and marrow biopsy lead to the diagnosis and it teaches hematologic reasoning.

triage.name: Appendicitis
triage.reason: Classic undifferentiated abdominal pain case with a clear diagnosis reachable by history, exam, labs and imaging, and important look-alikes.

triage.name: Arm Injuries and Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of arm harm rather than a single diagnosis; specific fractures or nerve injuries are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Arrhythmia
triage.reason: A broad category of rhythm disturbances rather than one diagnosis; specific rhythms such as atrial fibrillation are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Arsenic
triage.reason: A poisoning with GI, neurologic and dermatologic features that can be reached from exposure history and targeted testing.

triage.name: Arteriovenous Malformations
triage.reason: Can present with headache, seizure or hemorrhage; history, exam and imaging lead to a specific vascular malformation diagnosis.

triage.name: Arthritis
triage.reason: A broad category of joint inflammation rather than one diagnosis; specific arthritides such as gout or rheumatoid arthritis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Asbestos
triage.reason: An exposure or hazard topic rather than a patient diagnosis; the resulting diseases such as asbestosis or mesothelioma are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Aspergillosis
triage.reason: A fungal infection with pulmonary or disseminated presentations; history, imaging and microbiology lead to the diagnosis, often in immunocompromised patients.

triage.name: Asthma
triage.reason: Recurrent wheeze, cough and dyspnea with identifiable triggers; history, exam and spirometry lead to the diagnosis and it is a core ambulatory case.

triage.name: Asthma in Children
triage.reason: Classic pediatric presentation with recurrent wheeze, cough and dyspnea; diagnosis reachable by history, exam and spirometry, with important look-alikes such as bronchiolitis and foreign body.

triage.name: Ataxia Telangiectasia
triage.reason: Rare but distinctive neurocutaneous disorder: childhood-onset ataxia, conjunctival telangiectasias and recurrent sinopulmonary infections give a reachable diagnosis by history and exam.

triage.name: Atherosclerosis
triage.reason: A chronic pathologic process rather than a patient-presenting diagnosis; students meet its manifestations (angina, claudication, stroke) rather than atherosclerosis itself.

triage.name: Athlete's Foot
triage.reason: Common pruritic scaly rash of the feet with a clear diagnosis by history and exam, plus KOH testing; good for teaching dermatologic description and risk factors.

triage.name: Atrial Fibrillation
triage.reason: Very common arrhythmia presenting with palpitations, dyspnea or incidentally; diagnosis by ECG with rich teaching on stroke risk and rate/rhythm management.

triage.name: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
triage.reason: Common childhood behavioral presentation with inattention, impulsivity and hyperactivity; diagnosis reachable through structured history from parent and child, with school and developmental context.

triage.name: Autism Spectrum Disorder
triage.reason: Developmental presentation with impaired social communication and restricted repetitive behaviors; diagnosis by history and observation, with hearing and developmental screening in the workup.

triage.name: Autoimmune Diseases
triage.reason: A broad category of many distinct disorders, not a single diagnosis a student can reach; specific entities such as lupus or rheumatoid arthritis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Autonomic Nervous System Disorders
triage.reason: An umbrella category covering many distinct syndromes; no single coherent patient presentation, so specific diagnoses such as orthostatic hypotension are better case topics.

triage.name: Back Injuries
triage.reason: A mechanism-based category rather than a diagnosis; students reach specific entities such as lumbar strain or vertebral fracture, which are better case topics.

triage.name: Back Pain
triage.reason: Extremely common symptom presentation; workup centers on red flags and distinguishing mechanical pain from radiculopathy, malignancy or infection, making it a strong undifferentiated case.

triage.name: Bacterial Infections
triage.reason: A broad microbiologic category, not a single clinical diagnosis; specific infections such as cellulitis or pyelonephritis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Bad Breath
triage.reason: Common complaint with a focused differential (oral hygiene, gingival disease, sinus or GI causes); diagnosis largely by history and exam, though the presentation is less classic for a full case.

triage.name: Barotrauma
triage.reason: Pressure-related injury with a clear exposure history (flying, diving) and organ-specific findings such as ear pain, tympanic injury or pneumothorax; diagnosis by history and exam.

triage.name: Behcet's Syndrome
triage.reason: Rare multisystem vasculitis with recurrent oral and genital ulcers, uveitis and skin lesions; classic pattern-recognition case reachable by history and exam.

triage.name: Bell's Palsy
triage.reason: Acute unilateral facial paralysis with a clear presentation; key teaching is distinguishing it from stroke and other causes of facial weakness by exam.

triage.name: Benign Tumors
triage.reason: A broad category spanning many unrelated lesions; no single patient presentation, so specific tumors such as lipoma or uterine fibroids are better case topics.

triage.name: Bile Duct Cancer
triage.reason: Cholangiocarcinoma presents with painless jaundice, weight loss and cholestatic labs; diagnosis reachable by imaging and workup, with good teaching on obstructive jaundice.

triage.name: Bile Duct Diseases
triage.reason: An umbrella category covering stones, strictures, cholangitis and malignancy; specific diagnoses such as choledocholithiasis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Bipolar Disorder
triage.reason: Major psychiatric illness with manic or depressive episodes; diagnosis by careful history of mood episodes, sleep and function, with strong safety and differential teaching.

triage.name: Bird Flu
triage.reason: Rare but classic travel/exposure case: fever, respiratory symptoms, poultry contact, reachable by history and workup; important public-health look-alike.

triage.name: Birth Defects
triage.reason: Broad category of congenital malformations, not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Birth Weight
triage.reason: A measurement, not a diagnosis; no patient presentation to interview and work up.

triage.name: Birthmarks
triage.reason: Visible skin lesion with a differential (hemangioma, nevus, Mongolian spot) reachable by history and exam; good MSK & skin case.

triage.name: Bladder Cancer
triage.reason: Painless hematuria with smoking history; diagnosis reachable by history, urinalysis and cystoscopy workup.

triage.name: Bladder Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category of bladder pathology, not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Bleeding
triage.reason: A symptom/sign rather than a diagnosis; too broad to be a single case topic.

triage.name: Bleeding Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category covering many coagulopathies; not a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Blisters
triage.reason: A physical finding, not a diagnosis; the underlying cause is what would be worked up.

triage.name: Blood Clots
triage.reason: Broad concept (thrombosis/hypercoagulability) rather than a specific diagnosis; specific entities like DVT or PE are the case topics.

triage.name: Blood Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of hematologic disease, not a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Blood Transfusion and Donation
triage.reason: A care/therapy topic, not a diagnosis a student reaches by interviewing and examining a patient.

triage.name: Body Lice
triage.reason: Pruritic rash with identifiable lice/nits on exam; diagnosis reachable by history and physical, with good exposure and hygiene history.

triage.name: Body Weight
triage.reason: A measurement/wellness topic, not a diagnosis with a patient presentation.

triage.name: Bone Cancer
triage.reason: Bone pain or mass with imaging and biopsy workup; classic MSK malignancy case with a clear diagnostic path.

triage.name: Bone Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category of bone pathology, not a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Bone Infections
triage.reason: Osteomyelitis presents with focal bone pain, fever and risk factors; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, labs and imaging.

triage.name: Bone Marrow Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category of marrow pathology, not a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Botulism
triage.reason: Descending paralysis with foodborne or infant exposure history; classic neuro/emergency case with a clear diagnostic and exposure story.

triage.name: Bowel Incontinence
triage.reason: Fecal incontinence/encopresis presents with a clear history and exam, with a differential of organic and behavioral causes worth working up.

triage.name: Brachial Plexus Injuries
triage.reason: Focal neurologic deficit in the upper extremity reachable by history, exam and imaging/EMG; includes obstetric and traumatic forms with clear localization teaching.

triage.name: Brain Aneurysm
triage.reason: Thunderclap headache and sudden neurologic decline make a high-stakes emergency case; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, CT/LP and vascular imaging.

triage.name: Brain Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category term covering many unrelated brain conditions; not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Brain Malformations
triage.reason: Group of congenital structural anomalies rather than one presentation; too heterogeneous to build a single interviewable case.

triage.name: Brain Tumors
triage.reason: Headache with focal deficits or seizures is a classic case; students can localize the lesion and reach a diagnosis with imaging and pathology.

triage.name: Breast Cancer
triage.reason: Palpable breast mass or abnormal screening mammogram is a core case; diagnosis and staging reachable by history, exam, imaging and biopsy.

triage.name: Breast Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category covering benign and malignant breast conditions; not a single diagnosis a student can reach.

triage.name: Breathing Problems
triage.reason: Nonspecific symptom category (tachypnea) rather than a diagnosis; better represented by the underlying conditions.

triage.name: Bronchial Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of bronchial diseases; not a single interviewable diagnosis.

triage.name: Bruises
triage.reason: Nonspecific physical finding; the case would really be about the underlying cause (trauma, bleeding disorder, abuse), not the bruise itself.

triage.name: Burns
triage.reason: Clear mechanism and presentation; students assess depth, extent (TBSA), airway involvement and fluids, reaching a diagnosis and management plan.

triage.name: Bursitis
triage.reason: Focal joint-region pain and swelling reachable by history, exam and aspiration; good musculoskeletal differential teaching.

triage.name: C. diff Infections
triage.reason: Antibiotic-associated diarrhea with a clear exposure history; diagnosis reachable by history, exam and stool testing, with important severity assessment.

triage.name: Campylobacter Infections
triage.reason: Acute diarrheal illness with food/exposure history; students work through the infectious diarrhea differential and stool testing.

triage.name: Cancer
triage.reason: Umbrella term for all malignancies; too broad to be a single case. Specific cancers are the case-suitable units.

triage.name: Cancer Alternative Therapies
triage.reason: Care/treatment topic rather than a diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Cancer Chemotherapy
triage.reason: Treatment modality, not a patient presentation or diagnosis.

triage.name: Cancer Immunotherapy
triage.reason: Treatment modality rather than a diagnosis; not interviewable as a case.

triage.name: Cancer in Children
triage.reason: Broad category of pediatric malignancies; specific cancers (e.g. leukemia, neuroblastoma) are the case-suitable units.

triage.name: Cancer--Living with Cancer
triage.reason: Survivorship/care topic, not a diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Canker Sores
triage.reason: Recurrent painful oral ulcers with a recognizable history and exam; differential includes herpes, Behçet, and drug causes, so it works as a clinic case.

triage.name: Cannabis
triage.reason: Substance use presentation with intoxication, withdrawal, and cannabis hyperemesis; reachable by history and tox screen, though framed as a use disorder rather than a single disease.

triage.name: Carbohydrate Metabolism Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of inborn metabolic defects, not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interviewing and examining one patient.

triage.name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
triage.reason: Toxic exposure with headache, confusion, and possible syncope; diagnosis hinges on history of exposure and co-oximetry, a classic emergency case.

triage.name: Carcinoid Tumors
triage.reason: Neuroendocrine tumor presenting with flushing, diarrhea, or bowel obstruction; workup with labs and imaging is teachable, though presentation varies by site.

triage.name: Cardiomyopathy
triage.reason: Umbrella term covering dilated, hypertrophic, and restrictive forms with different presentations; too broad as a single case topic.

triage.name: Carotid Artery Disease
triage.reason: Often asymptomatic but can present with TIA or amaurosis fugax; history, exam, and vascular imaging make a solid stroke-prevention case.

triage.name: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
triage.reason: Nocturnal hand paresthesias with a positive Tinel/Phalen exam and confirmatory nerve study; classic outpatient musculoskeletal-neurology case.

triage.name: Cartilage Disorders
triage.reason: Pathological category of chondral tissue rather than a diagnosis reachable from a patient's history and workup.

triage.name: Cat Scratch Disease
triage.reason: Regional lymphadenopathy after a kitten scratch; history of exposure plus serology makes a clean infectious disease case with a good differential.

triage.name: Cataract
triage.reason: Progressive painless vision loss with an abnormal red reflex and slit-lamp findings; straightforward clinic presentation, though exam findings are specialty-specific.

triage.name: Celiac Disease
triage.reason: Malabsorption case with a clear diagnosis reachable by history, exam, serology and biopsy, plus important look-alikes.

triage.name: Cellulitis
triage.reason: Acute spreading skin infection with fever and erythema; diagnosis is clinical and mimics DVT and necrotizing infection, a strong teaching case.

triage.name: Cerebellar Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of cerebellar dysfunction with many causes; not a single diagnosis a student can reach from one patient encounter.

triage.name: Cerebral Palsy
triage.reason: Nonprogressive motor delay with spasticity and abnormal tone recognized in early childhood; pediatric history and exam drive the diagnosis.

triage.name: Cervical Cancer
triage.reason: Abnormal bleeding or postcoital spotting with an abnormal Pap and cervical lesion; screening, staging, and prevention make it a core ob/gyn case.

triage.name: Cervix Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of cervical pathology rather than a specific diagnosis with its own presentation.

triage.name: Chagas Disease
triage.reason: Chronic cardiomyopathy or achalasia in an immigrant patient from Latin America; exposure history plus serology and cardiac workup make a good case.

triage.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease
triage.reason: Slowly progressive distal weakness, foot deformity, and family history; exam and nerve conduction studies lead to the diagnosis.

triage.name: Chest Injuries and Disorders
triage.reason: Mixed category of chest trauma and rib fractures rather than a single diagnosis; too broad to build one case around.

triage.name: Chest Pain
triage.reason: Classic undifferentiated symptom with a broad, high-stakes differential (ACS, PE, dissection, GERD, musculoskeletal) reachable by history, exam, ECG and labs.

triage.name: Chiari Malformation
triage.reason: Congenital hindbrain malformation presenting with headache, neck pain, and neurologic deficits; diagnosis reachable via history, exam and MRI.

triage.name: Chickenpox
triage.reason: Highly recognizable exanthem with a classic prodrome and rash progression; diagnosis made clinically by history and exam.

triage.name: Chikungunya
triage.reason: Acute febrile illness with rash and severe polyarthralgia; diagnosis reachable by travel history, exam and serology, though rare in the US.

triage.name: Child Behavior Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of behavioral problems rather than a single diagnosis; too heterogeneous to build one interview-and-workup case around.

triage.name: Child Mental Health
triage.reason: Umbrella term for pediatric psychiatric illness, not a specific diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Child Nutrition
triage.reason: Broad nutritional-imbalance category (overnutrition/undernutrition) rather than a discrete diagnosis with a defined presentation.

triage.name: Childbirth Problems
triage.reason: Umbrella term for obstetric labor complications (breech, preterm labor, hemorrhage); too broad for a single case, though individual entities would work.

triage.name: Childhood Brain Tumors
triage.reason: Category of intracranial neoplasms rather than one diagnosis; specific tumor types would be case-suitable but the grouping is too broad.

triage.name: Childhood Leukemia
triage.reason: Grouping of leukemias by age rather than a single disease; specific subtypes (e.g. ALL) are case-suitable but this category is too broad.

triage.name: Chlamydia Infections
triage.reason: Common STI often asymptomatic or with urethritis/cervicitis; diagnosis reachable by sexual history, exam and NAAT testing.

triage.name: Choking
triage.reason: Acute airway obstruction event managed as an emergency; little diagnostic interview or differential workup, not a good case topic.

triage.name: Cholera
triage.reason: Profuse watery diarrhea with rapid dehydration; classic presentation reachable by travel history, exam and stool testing, though rare in the US.

triage.name: Cholesterol
triage.reason: A laboratory analyte/lipid abnormality rather than a diagnosis with a patient presentation; dyslipidemia management is a care topic.

triage.name: Cholesterol Levels: What You Need to Know
triage.reason: Patient-education topic about lipid testing, not a diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Cholesterol Medicines
triage.reason: Treatment/pharmacology topic (lipid-lowering drugs), not a patient presentation or diagnosis.

triage.name: Chronic Bronchitis
triage.reason: Chronic productive cough in a smoker; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, and spirometry, with a clear COPD differential.

triage.name: Chronic Kidney Disease
triage.reason: Progressive kidney dysfunction with fatigue, edema and lab abnormalities; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, urinalysis and creatinine-based staging.

triage.name: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia
triage.reason: Often incidental lymphocytosis with lymphadenopathy and fatigue; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, CBC and flow cytometry.

triage.name: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
triage.reason: Presents with fatigue, splenomegaly and marked leukocytosis; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, CBC and cytogenetics.

triage.name: Chronic Pain
triage.reason: A broad symptom category rather than a single diagnosis; the underlying cause is what a student would work up, so it does not make a focused case.

triage.name: Cirrhosis
triage.reason: Rich multisystem diagnosis reachable from history of alcohol or viral hepatitis, exam stigmata, and labs/imaging; classic complications to explore.

triage.name: Cleft Lip and Palate
triage.reason: Visible congenital anomaly with clear prenatal and postnatal presentation; good pediatric case for counseling and feeding issues.

triage.name: Cocaine
triage.reason: Substance use disorder with clear presentation, toxidrome, and complications; interview-driven diagnosis well suited to a case.

triage.name: Cold Sores
triage.reason: Common recognizable mucocutaneous infection with a straightforward history and exam diagnosis; good for primary care.

triage.name: Collapsed Lung
triage.reason: Acute presentation with dyspnea and chest pain; diagnosis reachable by exam and imaging, with important mimics.

triage.name: Colonic Diseases
triage.reason: A broad organ-based category, not a specific diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Colonic Polyps
triage.reason: Often asymptomatic but reachable via screening history and colonoscopy; good case for screening and cancer-risk counseling.

triage.name: Color Blindness
triage.reason: Hereditary vision defect detected by history and simple testing; reasonable pediatric or primary care case though limited workup.

triage.name: Colorectal Cancer
triage.reason: Common malignancy with clear presentation of bleeding, weight loss, and anemia; diagnosis reachable by history, exam, and colonoscopy.

triage.name: Coma
triage.reason: Altered mental status is a core undifferentiated presentation; students can reach a cause through history, exam, and targeted labs and imaging, though the patient cannot give history directly.

triage.name: Common Cold
triage.reason: Extremely common upper respiratory infection with classic history and exam; good for teaching viral URI and antibiotic stewardship.

triage.name: Common Infant and Newborn Problems
triage.reason: A broad category covering many unrelated newborn conditions rather than a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome
triage.reason: Distinctive post-injury pain syndrome with autonomic findings; diagnosis reachable by history and exam, good for pain and neuro teaching.

triage.name: Compulsive Gambling
triage.reason: Behavioral addiction with clear diagnostic criteria reachable by interview; good psychiatry case.

triage.name: Concussion
triage.reason: Common head injury with characteristic history and exam; diagnosis reachable clinically with important red flags to exclude.

triage.name: Congenital Heart Defects
triage.reason: A broad category of structural heart anomalies rather than one diagnosis; individual defects would be case-suitable.

triage.name: Connective Tissue Disorders
triage.reason: A heterogeneous group of disorders, not a single diagnosis; too broad for one case.

triage.name: Constipation
triage.reason: Very common symptom-based diagnosis reachable by history and exam; good for teaching red flags and secondary causes.

triage.name: COPD
triage.reason: Common chronic respiratory disease with classic smoking history, exam findings, and spirometry-confirmed diagnosis.

triage.name: Coping with Chronic Illness
triage.reason: A psychosocial/care concept rather than a diagnosis; no single patient presentation or workup leads to it.

triage.name: Corneal Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of eye disease, not a specific diagnosis a student reaches by interview and workup.

triage.name: Corns and Calluses

triage.name: Coronary Artery Disease

triage.name: Cough
triage.reason: Extremely common presenting symptom with a broad differential that students must narrow by history, exam and targeted testing.

triage.name: COVID-19 (Coronavirus Disease 2019)

triage.name: Craniofacial Abnormalities
triage.reason: Broad category of congenital malformations rather than one diagnosis; no single interview-and-workup path.

triage.name: Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease

triage.name: Crohn's Disease

triage.name: Croup
triage.reason: Classic pediatric presentation with barking cough and inspiratory stridor; diagnosis made clinically with important airway look-alikes.

triage.name: Cryptosporidiosis

triage.name: Cushing's Syndrome

triage.name: Cystic Fibrosis

triage.name: Cytomegalovirus Infections

triage.name: Dandruff, Cradle Cap, and Other Scalp Conditions

triage.name: Degenerative Nerve Diseases

triage.name: Dehydration

triage.name: Delirium

triage.name: Dementia

triage.name: Dengue

triage.name: Developmental Disabilities

triage.name: Diabetes

triage.name: Diabetes in Children and Teens

triage.name: Diabetic Heart Disease

triage.name: Diabetic Kidney Problems

triage.name: Diabetic Nerve Problems

triage.name: Diarrhea

triage.name: Digestive Diseases

triage.name: Diphtheria

triage.name: Dislocations

triage.name: Diverticulosis and Diverticulitis

triage.name: Dizziness and Vertigo

triage.name: Down Syndrome

triage.name: Drowning

triage.name: Drug Reactions

triage.name: Drugs and Young People

triage.name: Dry Mouth

triage.name: Dwarfism

triage.name: Dystonia

triage.name: E. coli Infections

triage.name: Ear Disorders

triage.name: Ear Infections

triage.name: Eating Disorders

triage.name: Ectopic Pregnancy

triage.name: Eczema

triage.name: Edema

triage.name: Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome

triage.name: Elbow Injuries and Disorders

triage.name: Electrical Injuries

triage.name: Emphysema

triage.name: Encephalitis

triage.name: End of Life Issues

triage.name: Endocarditis

triage.name: Endocrine Diseases

triage.name: Eosinophilic Disorders

triage.name: Eosinophilic Esophagitis

triage.name: Epilepsy

triage.name: Erectile Dysfunction
triage.reason: Common presenting complaint with vascular, endocrine, medication and psychogenic causes; diagnosis reachable by history, exam and targeted labs.

triage.name: Esophageal Cancer

triage.name: Esophagus Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of esophageal pathology, not a single diagnosis; specific entities such as achalasia or esophageal cancer are case-suitable.

triage.name: Eye Cancer

triage.name: Eye Care
triage.reason: A preventive and health-maintenance topic, not a diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Eye Diseases
triage.reason: A broad category covering all ocular pathology, not a single diagnosis; specific entities such as acute angle-closure glaucoma are case-suitable.

triage.name: Eye Infections

triage.name: Eye Injuries

triage.name: Eye Movement Disorders

triage.name: Eyelid Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of eyelid pathology, not a single diagnosis; specific entities such as hordeolum or blepharitis are case-suitable.

triage.name: Facial Injuries and Disorders

triage.name: Female Infertility

triage.name: Fetal Health and Development

triage.name: Fever

triage.name: Fibromyalgia

triage.name: Finger Injuries and Disorders

triage.name: Fistulas

triage.name: Fluid and Electrolyte Balance

triage.name: Food Allergy

triage.name: Foodborne Illness

triage.name: Foot Injuries and Disorders
triage.reason: Broad anatomic umbrella covering many distinct injuries and conditions; no single diagnosis or presentation.

triage.name: Foreign Bodies
triage.reason: Mechanistic category rather than a diagnosis; presentation varies entirely by site and object.

triage.name: Fractures
triage.reason: Generic injury category; a case needs a specific fracture (e.g., distal radius, hip, ankle) with its own presentation and workup.

triage.name: Fragile X Syndrome

triage.name: Friedreich Ataxia

triage.name: Frostbite

triage.name: Fungal Infections

triage.name: G6PD Deficiency

triage.name: Gallbladder Diseases

triage.name: Gallstones

triage.name: Gangrene

triage.name: Gas

triage.name: Gastroenteritis

triage.name: Gastrointestinal Bleeding
triage.reason: High-yield undifferentiated bleeding presentation with localization by history, exam, labs and endoscopy; strong clinical reasoning case.

triage.name: Gaucher Disease

triage.name: Genetic Brain Disorders

triage.name: Genetic Disorders
triage.reason: Umbrella category covering all inherited conditions; too broad to be a single case topic.

triage.name: Genital Warts

triage.name: GERD

triage.name: Giardia Infections

triage.name: Glaucoma

triage.name: Growth Disorders

triage.name: Gum Disease

triage.name: Haemophilus Infections

triage.name: Head Injuries

triage.name: Headache

triage.name: Health Problems in Pregnancy

triage.name: Hearing Disorders and Deafness

triage.name: Hearing Problems in Children

triage.name: Rh Incompatibility

triage.name: Rheumatoid Arthritis

triage.name: Rickets

triage.name: Rosacea

triage.name: Rotator Cuff Injuries

triage.name: Rotavirus Infections

triage.name: Rubella

triage.name: Safe Opioid Use

triage.name: Salivary Gland Cancer

triage.name: Salmonella Infections

triage.name: Sarcoidosis

triage.name: Scabies

triage.name: Scars

triage.name: Schizophrenia

triage.name: Sciatica

triage.name: Scleroderma

triage.name: Scoliosis

triage.name: Seasonal Affective Disorder

triage.name: Seizures

triage.name: Sepsis

triage.name: Sexual Problems in Men

triage.name: Shoulder Injuries and Disorders

triage.name: Sinusitis

triage.name: Sjogren's Syndrome

triage.name: Skin Cancer

triage.name: Skin Pigmentation Disorders

triage.name: Sleep Apnea

triage.name: Sleep Disorders

triage.name: Small Intestine Disorders

triage.name: Soft Tissue Sarcoma

triage.name: Sore Throat

triage.name: Speech and Communication Disorders

triage.name: Speech and Language Problems in Children
triage.reason: Broad category of developmental communication problems rather than a specific diagnosis; better modeled as individual conditions like language disorder or autism.

triage.name: Spider Bites

triage.name: Spina Bifida

triage.name: Spinal Cord Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category covering many distinct entities (myelopathy, tumors, infections); not a single diagnosis a student can reach.

triage.name: Spinal Cord Injuries
triage.reason: Traumatic myelopathy with a clear mechanism, exam findings and imaging; good for localization and acute management.

triage.name: Spinal Muscular Atrophy
triage.reason: Hereditary motor neuron disease with progressive weakness; diagnosis reachable via history, exam and genetic testing.

triage.name: Spinal Stenosis
triage.reason: Degenerative narrowing causing neurogenic claudication; classic history and exam with imaging confirmation and clear mimics.

triage.name: Spine Injuries and Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of vertebral fractures and disorders; not a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Spleen Diseases
triage.reason: Organ-based category covering many unrelated conditions; not a single patient-reachable diagnosis.

triage.name: Sports Injuries
triage.reason: Broad category of activity-related injuries rather than one diagnosis; individual injuries are better case topics.

triage.name: Sprains and Strains
triage.reason: Collective term for soft tissue injuries; too broad and nonspecific to be a single case diagnosis.

triage.name: Staphylococcal Infections
triage.reason: Organism-based category spanning skin, bloodstream and device infections; not one diagnosis.

triage.name: Steatotic Liver Disease
triage.reason: Common incidental abnormal liver enzymes or imaging finding; diagnosis reachable by history (alcohol, metabolic risk factors), exam, labs and imaging, with important distinctions between alcohol-associated and metabolic causes.

triage.name: Stillbirth
triage.reason: An outcome event rather than a diagnosis a student reaches by interviewing a patient; workup is of the mother and fetus.

triage.name: Stomach Cancer

triage.name: Stomach Disorders
triage.reason: Broad organ-based category covering many distinct conditions; not a single diagnosis.

triage.name: Streptococcal Infections
triage.reason: Organism-based category spanning pharyngitis, cellulitis and bacteremia; not one diagnosis.

triage.name: Stroke
triage.reason: Acute focal neurologic deficit with a time-critical workup and many mimics; excellent interview, exam and imaging case.

triage.name: Stuttering
triage.reason: Speech fluency disorder identified by history and observation; reachable diagnosis though management is largely non-medical.

triage.name: Sudden Cardiac Arrest
triage.reason: Dramatic presentation with loss of consciousness and pulselessness; students must recognize arrest, run the algorithm and identify reversible causes and the underlying cardiac or metabolic etiology.

triage.name: Sudden Infant Death Syndrome
triage.reason: A diagnosis of exclusion made after death; there is no living patient to interview or examine.

triage.name: Sun Exposure
triage.reason: A prevention/exposure topic rather than a diagnosis reachable by interview and workup; sunburn is a symptom-level finding, not a case-defining illness.

triage.name: Swallowing Disorders
triage.reason: Dysphagia is a common presenting complaint with a broad differential (neurologic vs mechanical) reachable by history, exam and testing.

triage.name: Syphilis
triage.reason: Classic staged infection with rich history, exam findings and serologic workup; important public health and look-alike teaching value.

triage.name: Syringomyelia
triage.reason: Distinctive dissociated sensory loss and myelopathic findings reachable by history, neurologic exam and MRI.

triage.name: Tailbone Disorders
triage.reason: Broad anatomic category rather than a specific diagnosis; coccydynia is a symptom and the grouping lacks a coherent case-defining presentation.

triage.name: Taste and Smell Disorders
triage.reason: Broad category of sensory dysfunction rather than a single diagnosis; workup is diffuse and presentation overlaps many causes.

triage.name: Tay-Sachs Disease
triage.reason: Infantile neurodegenerative presentation with developmental regression and cherry-red spot; classic pediatric genetics case.

triage.name: Tears
triage.reason: A normal physiologic secretion, not a diagnosis; no patient presentation to work up.

triage.name: Temporomandibular Disorders
triage.reason: Common facial pain syndrome with characteristic history and exam findings, reachable without advanced testing.

triage.name: Tendinitis
triage.reason: Common overuse injury with focal pain and exam findings; straightforward diagnosis with good differential teaching.

triage.name: Testicular Cancer
triage.reason: Young man with painless testicular mass; clear exam and imaging workup with important tumor marker teaching.

triage.name: Testicular Disorders
triage.reason: Broad organ-based category rather than a specific diagnosis; individual entities like torsion or epididymitis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Tetanus
triage.reason: Dramatic presentation with trismus, spasms and wound history; classic infectious disease case with prevention teaching.

triage.name: Thalassemia
triage.reason: Microcytic anemia with family history and characteristic labs; strong hematology teaching case with clear workup.

triage.name: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome
triage.reason: Positional arm symptoms with provocative maneuvers and imaging; good neurovascular differential case.

triage.name: Throat Cancer
triage.reason: Hoarseness, dysphagia and neck mass in a smoker; clear head and neck cancer workup with staging teaching.

triage.name: Throat Disorders
triage.reason: Broad anatomic category rather than a specific diagnosis; individual entities like pharyngitis are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Thymus Cancer
triage.reason: Mediastinal mass with myasthenia gravis association; distinctive imaging and paraneoplastic teaching.

triage.name: Thyroid Cancer
triage.reason: Thyroid nodule with characteristic exam and ultrasound/FNA workup; common and highly teachable.

triage.name: Thyroid Diseases
triage.reason: Broad organ-based category rather than a specific diagnosis; hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism are the case-suitable topics.

triage.name: Tick Bites
triage.reason: Patients present with a bite and concern for tick-borne illness; diagnosis is reachable by history, exam, and targeted testing, with important mimics and prevention counseling.

triage.name: Tinea Infections

triage.name: Tinnitus
triage.reason: A symptom patients describe directly; workup focuses on history, otoscopy, audiometry and excluding vascular or medication causes, making it a workable case.

triage.name: Tongue Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of many unrelated conditions rather than a single diagnosis a student can reach; too heterogeneous for one case.

triage.name: Tonsillitis

triage.name: Tooth Decay
triage.reason: Patients present with dental pain or sensitivity; diagnosis is reachable by history and exam, though definitive management is dental rather than medical.

triage.name: Tooth Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category covering many distinct dental conditions rather than one diagnosis; not a single interviewable case.

triage.name: Tourette Syndrome
triage.reason: Tics are observable and described by patients and families; diagnosis is clinical by history and exam, with comorbidity screening and behavioral treatment decisions.

triage.name: Toxoplasmosis

triage.name: Tracheal Disorders

triage.name: Transient Ischemic Attack

triage.name: Traumatic Brain Injury

triage.name: Tremor

triage.name: Trichomoniasis

triage.name: Trigeminal Neuralgia

triage.name: Triglycerides

triage.name: Tuberculosis

triage.name: Tuberous Sclerosis
triage.reason: Multisystem neurocutaneous disorder with skin findings, seizures and developmental delay; diagnosis is clinical with imaging and genetic confirmation.

triage.name: Tumors and Pregnancy
triage.reason: A co-occurrence category rather than a single diagnosis; management depends entirely on the specific cancer and gestational age.

triage.name: Turner Syndrome
triage.reason: Short stature, delayed puberty and characteristic exam findings lead to karyotype diagnosis; a classic genetics case with lifelong management.

triage.name: Ulcerative Colitis

triage.name: Uncommon Infant and Newborn Problems
triage.reason: A broad category of heterogeneous congenital and neonatal conditions, not a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Ureteral Disorders

triage.name: Urethral Disorders

triage.name: Urinary Incontinence

triage.name: Urinary Tract Infections

triage.name: Urine and Urination

triage.name: Usher Syndrome

triage.name: Uterine Cancer

triage.name: Uterine Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category encompassing many distinct uterine conditions rather than a single diagnosis.

triage.name: Uterine Fibroids

triage.name: Vaginal Bleeding

triage.name: Vaginal Cancer
triage.reason: Rare gynecologic malignancy presenting with abnormal bleeding or discharge; diagnosis reachable by exam and biopsy.

triage.name: Vaginal Diseases
triage.reason: Broad category of vaginal pathology rather than a single diagnosis; no single patient presentation.

triage.name: Vaginitis

triage.name: Valley Fever

triage.name: Varicose Veins

triage.name: Vascular Diseases

triage.name: Vasculitis

triage.name: Vision Impairment and Blindness

triage.name: Vitamin D Deficiency

triage.name: Vitiligo

triage.name: Voice Disorders

triage.name: Von Hippel-Lindau Disease
triage.reason: Rare inherited tumor syndrome with multi-organ manifestations; good for genetics and cancer surveillance reasoning.

triage.name: Vulvar Cancer
triage.reason: Gynecologic malignancy presenting with vulvar lesion or bleeding; diagnosis reachable by exam and biopsy.

triage.name: Vulvar Disorders
triage.reason: A broad category of vulvar conditions rather than a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup.

triage.name: Walking Problems

triage.name: Warts

triage.name: Weight Control
triage.reason: A care/wellness topic rather than a diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Weight Loss Surgery

triage.name: Whooping Cough

triage.name: Wilson Disease

triage.name: Winter Weather Emergencies

triage.name: Wounds and Injuries
triage.reason: A broad category of traumatic damage rather than a single diagnosis a student can reach by interview and workup.

triage.name: Wrist Injuries and Disorders

triage.name: Yeast Infections

triage.name: Zika Virus

triage.name: Unstable angina

triage.name: Aortic dissection

triage.name: Aortic stenosis

triage.name: Inflammatory bowel disease

triage.name: Trauma hemorrhage

triage.name: Postoperative fever

triage.reason: Young child with a seizure during fever is a common pediatric presentation where the diagnosis is reached by history and exam while excluding meningitis and other causes.

triage.name: Acute otitis media
triage.reason: Ear pain and fever in a child with a bulging erythematous tympanic membrane is a very common diagnosis reachable by history and otoscopy, with clear look-alikes.

triage.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis
triage.reason: Sore throat with fever, exudate and tender anterior cervical nodes is a very common presentation reachable by history, exam and rapid antigen testing.

triage.name: Hand, foot, and mouth disease
triage.reason: Child with fever, oral ulcers and vesicular rash on hands and feet is a common diagnosis reachable by history and exam alone.

triage.name: Neonatal jaundice
triage.reason: Yellow discoloration in a newborn is a very common presentation where history, exam and bilirubin testing distinguish physiologic from pathologic causes.

triage.name: Child abuse
triage.reason: Suspicious injuries inconsistent with the stated mechanism are a real diagnosis reachable through careful history, exam and imaging, with an important differential of accidental trauma and medical causes.

triage.name: Henoch-Schonlein purpura
triage.reason: Palpable purpura on the legs with abdominal pain and arthralgia in a child is a classic diagnosis reachable by history, exam, urinalysis and labs.

triage.name: Preeclampsia
triage.reason: New hypertension with proteinuria or end-organ symptoms after 20 weeks is a classic obstetric diagnosis reachable by history, exam, blood pressure and labs.

triage.name: Placental abruption
triage.reason: Painful vaginal bleeding with a tender, hypertonic uterus in late pregnancy is a classic obstetric emergency reachable by history, exam and ultrasound.

triage.name: Placenta previa
triage.reason: Painless vaginal bleeding in late pregnancy with a soft nontender uterus is a classic diagnosis reachable by history, exam and ultrasound, with a key look-alike in abruption.

triage.name: Postpartum hemorrhage
triage.reason: Acute obstetric emergency with a clear presentation (heavy bleeding after delivery) and a differential of uterine atony, retained placenta, lacerations and coagulopathy that students can work through.

triage.name: Hyperemesis gravidarum
triage.reason: Pregnancy-related vomiting with dehydration and weight loss; diagnosis is clinical and the differential (gastroenteritis, thyroid disease, molar pregnancy) is teachable.

triage.name: Ovarian torsion
triage.reason: Acute pelvic pain in a woman with a classic surgical emergency presentation; students can reach it by history, exam and imaging and must distinguish it from appendicitis and ectopic pregnancy.

triage.name: Bacterial vaginosis
triage.reason: Common vaginal discharge complaint with a characteristic history and office-based diagnosis; good for teaching vaginal discharge differential.

triage.name: Menopause
triage.reason: A normal physiologic life transition rather than a diagnosis reached by interview and workup; better framed as a care topic than a case.

triage.name: Major depressive disorder
triage.reason: Core psychiatric diagnosis made by structured history; students can elicit symptoms, assess safety and build a differential with bipolar and substance-related mood disorders.

triage.name: Opioid use disorder
triage.reason: Substance use diagnosis reachable by history; teaches screening, withdrawal assessment and differential from other causes of altered behavior.

triage.name: Suicidal ideation
triage.reason: A symptom-based presentation that students must assess and risk-stratify; interviewing and safety planning are the core skills, with a broad differential of contributing conditions.

triage.name: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
triage.reason: Rare but classic drug-induced syndrome with fever, rigidity and autonomic instability; a good differential against serotonin syndrome and catatonia.

triage.name: Serotonin syndrome
triage.reason: Drug-induced toxidrome with altered mental status, autonomic findings and clonus; students can identify it from medication history and exam and contrast it with NMS.

triage.name: Urinary tract infection
triage.reason: Extremely common presentation with dysuria and frequency; diagnosis is clinical with urinalysis and culture, and the differential includes vaginitis and urethritis.

triage.name: Tobacco use disorder
triage.reason: Substance use diagnosis identified by history; teaches dependence assessment and cessation counseling, though the presentation is less acute than other cases.

triage.name: Status epilepticus
triage.reason: Neurologic emergency with a clear presentation and a differential of causes (metabolic, toxic, structural) that students must work through while managing the patient.

triage.name: Spinal cord compression
triage.reason: Back pain with neurologic deficits; students can localize the lesion and build a differential of malignancy, abscess and fracture, with urgent imaging decisions.

triage.name: Acetaminophen poisoning
triage.reason: Classic toxicology case with an intentional or accidental overdose history, staged clinical course and a specific antidote; excellent for teaching toxidrome workup.

triage.name: Septic shock
triage.reason: High-acuity presentation with hypotension and organ dysfunction; students can identify sepsis, localize a source and recognize the shock physiology.

triage.name: Tension pneumothorax
triage.reason: Life-threatening respiratory emergency with a characteristic presentation and exam findings, reachable by history, exam and imaging, with important look-alikes.

triage.name: Acute asthma exacerbation
triage.reason: Common respiratory presentation with wheeze and dyspnea; students can grade severity, treat, and differentiate from COPD, anaphylaxis and foreign body.

triage.name: Hip fracture
triage.reason: Common injury in older adults presenting with hip pain and inability to bear weight; students can reach it by history, exam and imaging and consider the fall workup.

triage.name: Angioedema
triage.reason: Acute swelling presentation with a differential of allergic, hereditary and ACE-inhibitor causes; airway risk makes the history and exam high-yield.

triage.name: Upper airway obstruction
triage.reason: A patient with stridor, dyspnea and voice change is a recognizable presentation with a focused history, exam and workup that can localize the obstruction and identify its cause.

triage.name: Tinea versicolor
triage.reason: Common hypopigmented scaly rash diagnosed by history and exam with KOH prep confirmation; classic dermatology case with clear look-alikes.

triage.name: Molluscum contagiosum
triage.reason: Benign viral skin infection with characteristic umbilicated papules; diagnosis reachable by history and visual exam, common in children.

triage.name: Basal cell carcinoma
triage.reason: Most common skin cancer; classic pearly papule with telangiectasias on sun-exposed skin, diagnosed by exam and biopsy with important look-alikes.

triage.name: Squamous cell carcinoma of skin
triage.reason: Common keratinocyte carcinoma presenting as a scaly, crusted or ulcerated lesion on sun-exposed skin; diagnosed by exam and biopsy.

triage.name: Actinic keratosis
triage.reason: Very common sun-damaged skin lesion and precursor to squamous cell carcinoma; diagnosed clinically with characteristic rough scaly macules.

triage.name: Seborrheic keratosis
triage.reason: Extremely common benign skin growth with a classic stuck-on appearance; important to distinguish from melanoma and other pigmented lesions.

triage.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
triage.reason: Life-threatening drug-induced mucocutaneous reaction with clear exposure history, exam findings and dermatologic emergency management.

triage.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
triage.reason: Dramatic drug-induced mucocutaneous emergency with a clear diagnosis reachable by history of culprit drug exposure, exam showing skin detachment and mucosal involvement, and biopsy; important look-alikes include SJS and erythema multiforme.

triage.name: Erythema multiforme
triage.reason: Acute eruption with classic target lesions often after infection; diagnosed clinically and distinguished from SJS and urticaria.

triage.name: Pityriasis rosea
triage.reason: Self-limited exanthem with herald patch and Christmas-tree distribution; classic visual diagnosis with syphilis and tinea as look-alikes.

triage.name: Lichen planus
triage.reason: Pruritic papulosquamous disorder with classic purple flat-topped papules and oral involvement; diagnosed clinically with biopsy when needed.

triage.name: Folliculitis
triage.reason: Common inflammatory condition of hair follicles presenting with follicular papules and pustules; diagnosed clinically with clear risk factors.

triage.name: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome
triage.reason: Premature infant with grunting, retractions and cyanosis; diagnosis reachable from history, exam, blood gas and chest x-ray, with important look-alikes such as sepsis and transient tachypnea.

triage.name: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
triage.reason: Term or near-term infant, often after cesarean delivery, with early tachypnea that resolves; a classic neonatal respiratory distress look-alike reachable by history, exam and chest x-ray.

triage.name: Meconium aspiration syndrome
triage.reason: Infant born through meconium-stained fluid with respiratory distress and patchy infiltrates; diagnosis made from delivery history, exam, blood gas and imaging.

triage.name: Neonatal sepsis
triage.reason: Young infant with nonspecific instability, poor feeding and temperature instability; a core diagnosis reached by history, exam, cultures and CSF studies, with many mimics.

triage.name: Necrotizing enterocolitis
triage.reason: Premature infant with feeding intolerance, abdominal distension and bloody stools; diagnosis supported by abdominal x-ray showing pneumatosis, a classic surgical neonatal emergency.

triage.name: Neonatal hypoglycemia
triage.reason: Infant of a diabetic mother or growth-restricted infant with jitteriness, lethargy or poor feeding; a very common problem diagnosed by bedside glucose with a broad differential.

triage.name: Neonatal abstinence syndrome
triage.reason: Infant with irritability, high-pitched cry, tremor and feeding problems whose mother used opioids in pregnancy; diagnosis is clinical from maternal and infant history.

triage.name: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy
triage.reason: Newborn with a sentinel perinatal event, low Apgar scores and encephalopathy; diagnosis from delivery history, exam, blood gas and imaging, with therapeutic implications.

triage.name: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia
triage.reason: Premature infant who remains oxygen-dependent weeks after birth; a chronic neonatal lung disease diagnosed from the clinical course and imaging, though less of a single-visit puzzle.

triage.name: Retinopathy of prematurity
triage.reason: Premature infant found on screening fundoscopic exam; diagnosis is made by eye exam rather than interview, so it is a weaker but still usable case.

triage.name: Intraventricular hemorrhage of newborn
triage.reason: Premature infant with apnea, lethargy or a drop in hematocrit; diagnosed by cranial ultrasound, an important cause of neonatal neurologic deterioration.

triage.name: Congenital hypothyroidism
triage.reason: Infant with prolonged jaundice, constipation, poor feeding and hypotonia; classically detected on newborn screening, and a treatable cause of developmental delay.

triage.name: Hirschsprung disease
triage.reason: Infant with delayed meconium passage, abdominal distension and chronic constipation; diagnosis reached by history, exam, contrast enema and rectal biopsy.

triage.name: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis
triage.reason: Weeks-old infant with progressive nonbilious projectile vomiting and a palpable olive; classic diagnosis from history, exam, electrolytes and ultrasound.

triage.name: Esophageal atresia
triage.reason: Newborn with excessive secretions, choking and cyanosis with feeds; diagnosed by failure to pass a feeding tube and imaging, often with a tracheoesophageal fistula.

triage.name: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia
triage.reason: Newborn with severe respiratory distress, a scaphoid abdomen and bowel sounds in the chest; diagnosed by exam and chest x-ray, a classic neonatal emergency.

triage.name: Gastroschisis
triage.reason: Newborn with bowel protruding through an abdominal wall defect lateral to the umbilicus; obvious on exam and a surgical emergency, though less of a diagnostic puzzle.

triage.name: Developmental dysplasia of the hip
triage.reason: Infant with asymmetric thigh folds or a positive Ortolani/Barlow maneuver; diagnosed by exam and ultrasound, a core pediatric screening topic.

triage.name: Neonatal herpes simplex
triage.reason: Young infant with vesicular skin lesions, lethargy or seizures; a high-stakes diagnosis reached by history, exam, and HSV PCR of surface sites, blood and CSF.

triage.name: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection
triage.reason: Infant with petechiae, jaundice, microcephaly or hearing loss; diagnosed by urine or saliva CMV testing, an important congenital infection with lasting sequelae.

triage.name: Ophthalmia neonatorum
triage.reason: Neonatal eye discharge with a clear differential by timing and organism; reachable via history, exam and conjunctival cultures.

triage.name: Kwashiorkor
triage.reason: Edematous protein-energy malnutrition with classic skin, hair and edema findings; a student can reach it from diet history and exam.

triage.name: Marasmus
triage.reason: Severe wasting from inadequate energy intake; diagnosis is clinical from growth and dietary history with a recognizable exam.

triage.name: Scurvy
triage.reason: Dietary vitamin C deficiency with gingival bleeding, perifollicular hemorrhage and poor wound healing; classic history-plus-exam diagnosis.

triage.name: Beriberi
triage.reason: Thiamine deficiency presenting with neuropathy, high-output heart failure or edema; reachable from diet and alcohol history plus exam.

triage.name: Wernicke encephalopathy
triage.reason: Acute confusional state with ophthalmoplegia and ataxia in a malnourished or alcohol-using patient; a high-yield interview and exam diagnosis.

triage.name: Vitamin B12 deficiency
triage.reason: Megaloblastic anemia with neuropathy; diagnosis reachable from diet, medication and surgical history plus labs.

triage.name: Folate deficiency anemia
triage.reason: Megaloblastic anemia from poor intake, alcohol or pregnancy; a straightforward history and lab-based diagnosis with important look-alikes.

triage.name: Pellagra
triage.reason: Niacin deficiency with dermatitis, diarrhea and dementia; distinctive sun-exposed rash plus diet history makes it a reachable diagnosis.

triage.name: Vitamin A deficiency
triage.reason: Night blindness and xerophthalmia with dietary history; exam findings are distinctive though the classic presentation is outside the US.

triage.name: Vitamin K deficiency bleeding
triage.reason: Bleeding with prolonged PT in a newborn or malabsorbing adult; diagnosis reachable from bleeding history, exam and coagulation labs.

triage.name: Zinc deficiency
triage.reason: Acrodermatitis-like rash, diarrhea, poor wound healing and hypogeusia; a diet- and exam-based diagnosis with recognizable skin findings.

triage.name: Refeeding syndrome
triage.reason: Electrolyte derangement after refeeding a malnourished patient; a student can reach it from the feeding history and metabolic labs.

triage.name: Iodine deficiency
triage.reason: A population-level nutritional deficiency usually detected by screening; it has no characteristic patient presentation a student can interview and work up.

triage.name: Short bowel syndrome
triage.reason: Malabsorption and diarrhea after massive bowel resection; diagnosis follows from surgical history, nutrition exam and absorption labs.

triage.name: Failure to thrive
triage.reason: Poor growth in an infant with a broad differential; a student can work it up through feeding history, growth chart and exam.

triage.name: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
triage.reason: Sudden painful red eye with halos and a fixed mid-dilated pupil; classic emergency presentation reachable by history, exam and tonometry.

triage.name: Primary open-angle glaucoma
triage.reason: Asymptomatic progressive vision loss found on exam and screening; a student can reach it from risk factors, optic disc exam and tonometry.

triage.name: Central retinal artery occlusion
triage.reason: Sudden painless monocular vision loss with a cherry-red spot; a stroke-like emergency reachable by history, fundoscopy and workup.

triage.name: Central retinal vein occlusion
triage.reason: Sudden painless vision loss with diffuse retinal hemorrhages; reachable from vascular risk history, fundoscopy and workup.

triage.name: Bacterial conjunctivitis
triage.reason: Common red eye presentation with discharge; diagnosis reachable by history, exam and, when needed, cultures, with important look-alikes such as viral and allergic conjunctivitis.

triage.name: Corneal abrasion
triage.reason: Acute painful red eye after trauma or foreign body; classic history and exam with fluorescein staining make a good case with look-alikes like corneal ulcer and uveitis.

triage.name: Hordeolum
triage.reason: Focal painful eyelid swelling diagnosed by inspection and history; good dermatology/primary care case with chalazion as the main look-alike.

triage.name: Chalazion
triage.reason: Painless eyelid nodule distinguished from hordeolum by history and exam; a straightforward but instructive eyelid lesion case.

triage.name: Orbital cellulitis
triage.reason: Serious orbital infection with proptosis, pain with eye movement and vision change; high-stakes emergency case distinguished from preseptal cellulitis by exam and imaging.

triage.name: Periorbital cellulitis
triage.reason: Eyelid and preseptal swelling after local trauma or sinusitis; diagnosis by history and exam, with orbital cellulitis as the critical look-alike.

triage.name: Anterior uveitis
triage.reason: Painful red eye with photophobia and decreased vision; slit-lamp findings and association with systemic disease make a rich case with several look-alikes.

triage.name: Optic neuritis
triage.reason: Subacute monocular vision loss with pain on eye movement; classic neuro-ophthalmology case with strong link to demyelinating disease and clear look-alikes.

triage.name: Frailty
triage.reason: A geriatric syndrome defined by accumulated deficits rather than a single diagnosis reachable by interview and workup; better taught as a concept than as a case.

triage.name: Sarcopenia
triage.reason: An age-related loss of muscle mass and function, generally a chronic finding rather than a diagnosis students reach through a focused interview and workup.

triage.name: Orthostatic hypotension
triage.reason: A physical finding defined by a blood pressure drop on standing, not a disease; it is a sign of many underlying causes rather than a case diagnosis itself.

triage.name: Normal pressure hydrocephalus
triage.reason: Classic triad of gait disturbance, cognitive decline and incontinence in an older adult; diagnosis by history, exam and imaging, with several dementia look-alikes.

triage.name: Fecal impaction
triage.reason: Abdominal pain, distension and inability to pass stool; diagnosed by history, exam and imaging, with bowel obstruction and constipation as look-alikes.

triage.name: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
triage.reason: Family history, flank pain, hematuria and hypertension with characteristic imaging; a strong genetics and nephrology case with clear diagnostic criteria.

triage.name: IgA nephropathy
triage.reason: Episodic gross hematuria after upper respiratory infection in a young adult; classic nephrology case with biopsy-based diagnosis and several glomerulonephritis look-alikes.

triage.name: Minimal change disease
triage.reason: Sudden nephrotic syndrome with edema and proteinuria, especially in children; diagnosis by history, labs and biopsy, with other nephrotic syndromes as look-alikes.

triage.name: Membranous nephropathy
triage.reason: Adult nephrotic syndrome with edema and heavy proteinuria; biopsy-based diagnosis with secondary causes and other nephrotic syndromes as look-alikes.

triage.name: Renal tubular acidosis
triage.reason: Non-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with characteristic electrolyte patterns; a good acid-base reasoning case worked out from labs and history.

triage.name: Metabolic acidosis
triage.reason: An acid-base derangement rather than a specific diagnosis; it is a finding that prompts a search for its cause, so it works better as a lab concept than a case.

triage.name: Hypokalemia
triage.reason: An electrolyte abnormality with many causes rather than a disease; students should learn to work up the underlying cause, so it is a poor stand-alone case topic.

triage.name: Hypernatremia
triage.reason: Electrolyte disturbance with a clear presentation (thirst, confusion, volume status) reachable by history, exam and labs; good teaching on free water deficit and look-alikes.

triage.name: Hypomagnesemia
triage.reason: Common electrolyte abnormality that presents with nonspecific symptoms and arrhythmias; diagnosis is made by history, medication review and serum magnesium.

triage.name: Rhabdomyolysis
triage.reason: Acute presentation with muscle pain, weakness and dark urine after a trigger; classic case with clear labs (CK, myoglobin) and important complications to recognize.
triage.category: muscle injury / acute kidney injury risk

triage.name: Contrast-induced nephropathy
triage.reason: Iatrogenic cause of acute kidney injury with a recognizable timeline after contrast exposure; students can work through risk factors, urinalysis and creatinine trend.

triage.name: Renal artery stenosis
triage.reason: Secondary hypertension case with clues on history (resistant hypertension, bruit, flash pulmonary edema) and imaging workup; good differential with essential hypertension.

triage.name: Drug allergy
triage.reason: Broad category rather than a single diagnosis; overlaps with specific reactions (penicillin allergy, serum sickness) and is better taught as those entities.

triage.name: Penicillin allergy
triage.reason: Very common clinical problem with a clear history-based assessment (timing, symptoms, reaction type) and important implications for antibiotic choice.

triage.name: Hereditary angioedema
triage.reason: Recurrent non-urticarial swelling with abdominal attacks and family history; distinctive presentation reachable by history and complement studies.

triage.name: Common variable immunodeficiency
triage.reason: Recurrent sinopulmonary infections and low immunoglobulins; diagnosis reached by infection history, immunoglobulin levels and vaccine responses.

triage.name: Selective IgA deficiency
triage.reason: Often asymptomatic but can present with recurrent infections, GI disease or transfusion reactions; diagnosed by immunoglobulin testing.

triage.name: Allergic conjunctivitis
triage.reason: Itchy watery red eyes with seasonal triggers; diagnosis is clinical from history and exam, with good look-alikes (viral, bacterial, dry eye).

triage.name: Allergic contact dermatitis
triage.reason: Pruritic eczematous rash with a clear exposure history and distribution; diagnosed by pattern recognition and patch testing.

triage.name: Serum sickness
triage.reason: Fever, urticaria, arthralgias and lymphadenopathy days after a new drug; classic immune-complex reaction reachable by exposure history and exam.

triage.name: Epididymitis
triage.reason: Acute scrotal pain with gradual onset and urinary symptoms; key differential with testicular torsion, worked up by history, exam, urinalysis and ultrasound.

triage.name: Acute pyelonephritis
triage.reason: Fever, flank pain and urinary symptoms with a clear diagnostic path (urinalysis, culture, imaging when complicated); important look-alikes.

triage.name: Acute prostatitis
triage.reason: Fever, dysuria, perineal pain and tender prostate on exam; diagnosed clinically with urine testing, with a clear differential.

triage.name: Renal cell carcinoma
triage.reason: Often incidental but can present with hematuria, flank mass and paraneoplastic findings; imaging-based diagnosis with a teachable differential.

triage.name: Acute urinary retention
triage.reason: Painful inability to void with a palpable bladder; a classic emergency presentation with clear diagnosis and important causes to differentiate.

triage.name: Hydronephrosis
triage.reason: Radiographic finding rather than a single diagnosis; better taught through its underlying causes (obstruction, stones, tumors) than as a standalone case.

triage.name: Varicocele
triage.reason: Scrotal swelling with a characteristic bag-of-worms exam finding; diagnosed clinically and by ultrasound, with infertility implications.

triage.name: Hydrocele
triage.reason: Common scrotal swelling that students can diagnose by history and exam (transillumination) with ultrasound to confirm, and distinguish from hernia, varicocele and tumor.

triage.name: Phimosis
triage.reason: A focused genitourinary complaint diagnosed largely by history and inspection of the foreskin, with important distinction from paraphimosis and balanitis.

triage.name: Cryptorchidism
triage.reason: Pediatric genital exam finding reachable by history and physical exam, with clear workup and management decisions including timing of orchiopexy.

triage.name: Neurogenic bladder
triage.reason: Urinary symptoms with a clear neurologic cause; students can build the picture from history, exam and urodynamic/post-void residual testing, though it is a syndrome rather than a single disease.

triage.name: Hepatic encephalopathy
triage.reason: Altered mental status in a patient with liver disease or portosystemic shunting supports a clinical diagnosis after evaluating alternative causes and precipitants.

triage.name: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis
triage.reason: A patient with ascites and abdominal symptoms, fever, or unexplained deterioration offers a focused diagnostic case established by diagnostic paracentesis.

triage.name: Alcoholic hepatitis
triage.reason: Recent jaundice, a detailed alcohol history, characteristic laboratory findings, and exclusion of competing causes provide a strong clinical diagnostic case.

triage.name: Pseudogout
triage.reason: Acute inflammatory arthritis can be evaluated by history, joint examination, and synovial fluid analysis while excluding septic arthritis.

triage.name: Immune thrombocytopenia
triage.reason: Petechiae or mucosal bleeding with isolated thrombocytopenia supports a diagnosis reached through blood counts, smear review, and exclusion of secondary causes.

triage.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
triage.reason: Thrombocytopenia and microangiopathic hemolytic anemia create an urgent diagnostic case requiring immediate recognition and treatment without waiting for ADAMTS13 results.

triage.name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
triage.reason: A platelet fall or new thrombosis after heparin exposure supports a case built around exposure timing, clinical probability assessment, and appropriate antibody testing.

triage.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
triage.reason: Bleeding or thrombosis in an appropriate underlying illness can be evaluated using platelet counts, coagulation studies, fibrinogen, and fibrin degradation markers.

triage.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism
triage.reason: Hypertension, sometimes with hypokalemia, provides a diagnostic case using aldosterone and renin testing followed by appropriately selected confirmation and subtype evaluation.

triage.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
triage.reason: Hypercalcemia, kidney stones, or skeletal symptoms can lead to a biochemical diagnosis using calcium and parathyroid hormone measurements and evaluation of mimics.

triage.name: Mitral regurgitation
triage.reason: A characteristic murmur, with or without dyspnea or heart failure findings, leads to echocardiographic confirmation and assessment of severity and cause.

triage.name: Atrial flutter
triage.reason: Palpitations, dyspnea, or incidental tachycardia can be evaluated by examination and ECG to distinguish flutter from other supraventricular arrhythmias.

triage.name: Complete heart block
triage.reason: Syncope, fatigue, or symptomatic bradycardia creates a high-yield case diagnosed by ECG, with immediate assessment of hemodynamic stability and reversible causes.

triage.name: Acute interstitial nephritis
triage.reason: Acute kidney injury with a relevant medication or systemic illness history supports a diagnostic workup using urinalysis, exclusion of alternatives, and biopsy when needed.

triage.name: Thyroid storm
triage.reason: Severe thyrotoxicosis with fever and systemic decompensation provides an urgent clinical diagnosis supported by thyroid testing, without delaying treatment for results.

triage.name: Myxedema coma
triage.reason: Altered mental status, hypothermia, and systemic decompensation from severe hypothyroidism form an emergency case requiring prompt clinical recognition and supportive testing.

triage.name: COPD exacerbation
triage.reason: Acute worsening of dyspnea, cough, or sputum in a patient with COPD supports a clinical case that evaluates severity, triggers, and alternative cardiopulmonary diagnoses.

triage.name: Pleural effusion
triage.reason: Although a manifestation rather than an underlying cause, pleural effusion is a concrete diagnosis reachable through examination and imaging, with fluid analysis when indicated.

triage.name: Lung abscess
triage.reason: Fever, productive cough, and relevant aspiration risks lead to chest imaging showing a cavitary infection, with evaluation for malignancy and other infectious causes.

triage.name: Bronchiectasis
triage.reason: Chronic productive cough and recurrent respiratory infections provide a diagnostic case confirmed by chest CT, followed by evaluation of underlying causes.

triage.name: Autoimmune hemolytic anemia
triage.reason: Fatigue, jaundice and anemia lead to a hemolysis workup, with direct antiglobulin testing supporting an immune cause.

triage.name: Polycythemia vera
triage.reason: Erythrocytosis, pruritus or thrombosis prompts evaluation with erythropoietin levels, JAK2 testing and often bone marrow examination.

triage.name: Sigmoid volvulus
triage.reason: Abdominal distention, pain and obstipation create a recognizable large-bowel obstruction case confirmed by imaging.

triage.name: Incarcerated inguinal hernia
triage.reason: An irreducible groin bulge, sometimes with bowel obstruction, is diagnosed by examination with imaging when needed and assessment for strangulation.

triage.name: Acute cholangitis
triage.reason: Fever, abdominal pain and evidence of biliary obstruction support a focused laboratory and imaging workup for an urgent biliary infection.

triage.name: Gallstone pancreatitis
triage.reason: Acute epigastric pain and elevated lipase establish pancreatitis, while liver tests and biliary imaging help identify gallstones as the cause.

triage.name: Anal fissure
triage.reason: Pain with defecation and small-volume bright red bleeding lead to a diagnosis usually established by gentle inspection.

triage.name: Perianal abscess
triage.reason: Focal perianal pain, swelling and tenderness support clinical diagnosis; imaging helps when a deeper or occult abscess is suspected.

triage.name: Pilonidal disease
triage.reason: Natal cleft pits, drainage or a painful abscess provide a characteristic history and examination-based diagnosis.

triage.name: Splenic rupture
triage.reason: Trauma or a predisposing illness with abdominal pain and possible hemorrhagic shock supports a case using stability-guided ultrasound or CT evaluation.

triage.name: Hemothorax
triage.reason: Chest trauma, dyspnea and reduced breath sounds lead to bedside assessment and imaging for blood in the pleural space.

triage.name: Surgical wound infection
triage.reason: Postoperative wound pain, erythema or drainage supports evaluation for surgical site infection and distinction from deeper infection or noninfectious wound complications.

triage.name: Thyroid nodule
triage.reason: A palpable or incidentally detected thyroid lesion has a structured workup using TSH, ultrasound and risk-guided biopsy or radionuclide imaging.

triage.name: Achalasia
triage.reason: Dysphagia to solids and liquids with regurgitation prompts endoscopic exclusion of obstruction and confirmation with esophageal manometry.

triage.name: Boerhaave syndrome
triage.reason: Severe chest or upper abdominal pain after forceful vomiting creates an urgent diagnostic case requiring evaluation for esophageal perforation.

triage.name: Toxic megacolon
