triage.reason: Severe colitis with systemic toxicity and radiographic colonic dilation supports a distinct emergency diagnosis and assessment for perforation.

triage.name: Acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
triage.reason: Acute colonic distention in a hospitalized or postoperative patient prompts imaging to exclude mechanical obstruction and evaluate complications.

triage.name: Biliary colic
triage.reason: Episodic right upper quadrant or epigastric pain with gallstones on ultrasound allows differentiation from cholecystitis, cholangitis and pancreatitis.

triage.name: Umbilical hernia
triage.reason: An umbilical bulge is usually diagnosed by examination, with assessment of reducibility and symptoms distinguishing uncomplicated disease from incarceration.

triage.name: Breast abscess
triage.reason: A painful focal breast mass with inflammatory findings prompts ultrasound to identify a drainable collection and distinguish abscess from mastitis alone.

triage.name: Fibroadenoma of breast
triage.reason: A palpable breast mass supports a focused history, breast examination, age-appropriate imaging and tissue sampling when indicated.

triage.name: Carotid artery stenosis
triage.reason: Transient monocular vision loss or focal neurologic symptoms can prompt vascular imaging that identifies symptomatic carotid stenosis; a bruit alone is not diagnostic.

triage.name: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
triage.reason: Adolescent hip or referred knee pain, limp and restricted hip internal rotation lead to diagnostic radiographs and urgent orthopedic assessment.

triage.name: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease
triage.reason: A child with an atraumatic limp, hip or knee pain and restricted hip motion can be evaluated with radiographs for femoral head osteonecrosis.

triage.name: Transient synovitis of hip
triage.reason: Acute childhood limp and hip pain support a clinical diagnosis after appropriate assessment for septic arthritis and other serious causes.

triage.name: Nursemaid's elbow
triage.reason: A young child refusing to use an arm after traction has a characteristic examination; atypical findings prompt evaluation for fracture.

triage.name: Foreign body aspiration
triage.reason: Choking history, sudden cough or wheezing, asymmetric breath sounds, and targeted imaging support diagnosis; bronchoscopy can confirm and remove the object even when radiographs are normal.

triage.name: Scarlet fever
triage.reason: Fever, pharyngitis and a characteristic sandpaper-like rash lead to testing for group A streptococcal infection.

triage.name: Ventricular septal defect
triage.reason: A characteristic murmur, or feeding difficulty and poor growth with a larger shunt, leads to echocardiographic diagnosis.

triage.name: Tetralogy of Fallot
triage.reason: Cyanosis, a systolic murmur or hypercyanotic episodes provide a recognizable presentation confirmed by echocardiography.

triage.name: Vesicoureteral reflux
triage.reason: Selected children with recurrent febrile urinary infections or abnormal urinary tract imaging undergo voiding cystourethrography to establish the diagnosis.

triage.name: Biliary atresia
triage.reason: Persistent infant jaundice, pale stools and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia prompt urgent hepatobiliary evaluation and definitive assessment.

triage.name: Infantile colic
triage.reason: Recurrent prolonged crying in an otherwise healthy, growing infant is assessed through history and examination while excluding illness or injury; intestinal obstruction is not its defining cause.

triage.name: Roseola infantum
triage.reason: Several days of high fever followed by a truncal rash as the fever resolves form a characteristic clinical diagnosis in infants and toddlers.

triage.name: Patent ductus arteriosus
triage.reason: A continuous murmur, bounding pulses or cardiopulmonary symptoms in an infant prompt echocardiography to identify a persistent ductal connection.

triage.name: Coarctation of the aorta
triage.reason: Upper-extremity hypertension, weak femoral pulses or neonatal circulatory collapse lead to limb blood pressure comparison and confirmatory cardiovascular imaging.

triage.name: Osgood-Schlatter disease
triage.reason: Activity-related anterior knee pain and focal tibial tubercle tenderness in a growing adolescent usually permit clinical diagnosis.

triage.name: Eclampsia
triage.reason: New-onset seizures during pregnancy or postpartum require immediate stabilization and evaluation for eclampsia and alternative causes; previously recognized preeclampsia is not required.

triage.name: HELLP syndrome
triage.reason: Pregnancy or postpartum right upper quadrant pain, nausea or malaise prompts evaluation for hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia.

triage.name: Prelabor rupture of membranes
triage.reason: Leakage of vaginal fluid before labor is evaluated with sterile speculum examination and appropriate fluid testing; gestational age distinguishes term PROM from preterm PROM.

triage.name: Primary amenorrhea
triage.reason: A defined clinical presentation with a structured diagnostic evaluation using pubertal history, examination, pregnancy testing, hormone studies and pelvic imaging.

triage.name: Chorioamnionitis
triage.reason: An important intrapartum infection recognized through maternal fever, associated clinical findings and assessment for alternative sources of fever.

triage.name: Postpartum endometritis
triage.reason: A clinical diagnosis supported by postpartum fever, uterine tenderness and obstetric risk factors, with evaluation for other causes of postpartum fever.

triage.name: Hydatidiform mole
triage.reason: A distinct pregnancy disorder evaluated with bleeding history, examination, quantitative hCG and ultrasound, with histopathologic confirmation after evacuation.

triage.name: Ruptured ovarian cyst
triage.reason: A useful acute pelvic pain case requiring pregnancy testing, assessment of hemodynamic stability and ultrasound to distinguish ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion.

triage.name: Tubo-ovarian abscess
triage.reason: A pelvic infection diagnosed through pain and fever history, pelvic examination and imaging, with important distinctions from ectopic pregnancy, torsion and appendicitis.

triage.name: Cervical insufficiency
triage.reason: A recognizable obstetric diagnosis based on characteristic pregnancy-loss history or painless second-trimester cervical dilation, supported by examination and ultrasound.

triage.name: Uterine rupture
triage.reason: A time-critical obstetric diagnosis suspected from labor history, fetal heart rate abnormalities and maternal findings; urgent surgery must not be delayed for confirmatory imaging.

triage.name: Shoulder dystocia
triage.reason: A specific delivery complication diagnosed directly when the shoulders fail to deliver with usual gentle traction after the head; recognition is clinical and requires immediate action.

triage.name: Bartholin gland cyst
triage.reason: A localized vulvar mass diagnosed primarily by history and examination, with useful distinctions from abscess and other vulvar lesions.

triage.name: Schizoaffective disorder
triage.reason: A longitudinal psychiatric diagnosis requiring careful mapping of mood episodes and psychosis, collateral history and exclusion of substance-induced or medical causes.

triage.name: Brief psychotic disorder
triage.reason: An acute psychosis case requiring symptom chronology and exclusion of medical, substance-related and mood causes; the diagnosis requires recovery within one month.

triage.name: Delusional disorder
triage.reason: A distinct psychiatric diagnosis evaluated through persistent delusions, relatively preserved functioning outside their effects and exclusion of other psychiatric, substance and medical causes.

triage.name: Persistent depressive disorder
triage.reason: A chronic mood disorder diagnosed through symptom duration, functional effects and assessment for bipolar disorder, substance effects and medical contributors.

triage.name: Social anxiety disorder
triage.reason: A common anxiety diagnosis reached through persistent fear of social scrutiny, avoidance and impairment, distinguished from ordinary shyness and other anxiety disorders.

triage.name: Acute stress disorder
triage.reason: A trauma-related diagnosis based on qualifying exposure, symptoms lasting three days to one month and functional impairment, distinguished from PTSD and expected early stress reactions.

triage.name: Adjustment disorder
triage.reason: A clinical diagnosis linking distress or impairment to an identifiable stressor while excluding another mental disorder and an expected, culturally appropriate response.

triage.name: Binge eating disorder
triage.reason: A specific eating disorder diagnosed through recurrent distressing binges with loss of control and without regular compensatory behaviors, distinguished from bulimia and ordinary overeating.

triage.name: Borderline personality disorder
triage.reason: A longitudinal diagnosis based on pervasive instability in relationships, self-image and emotion regulation, requiring assessment of impulsivity, self-harm risk and competing diagnoses.

triage.name: Antisocial personality disorder
triage.reason: An adult personality disorder diagnosed through a pervasive pattern of violating others' rights, developmental evidence of conduct disorder and collateral history when available.

triage.name: Alcohol withdrawal
triage.reason: Recent reduction in sustained alcohol use, autonomic symptoms and tremor support a clinical diagnosis while assessing seizure risk and excluding competing causes.

triage.name: Delirium tremens
triage.reason: Withdrawal-associated delirium and marked autonomic hyperactivity create an urgent diagnostic case requiring exclusion of other causes of delirium.

triage.name: Opioid withdrawal
triage.reason: Opioid cessation followed by characteristic gastrointestinal, autonomic and behavioral findings permits a clinical diagnosis and assessment for mimics.

triage.name: Lithium toxicity
triage.reason: Medication history, gastrointestinal or neurologic findings, serum lithium levels and renal assessment support a concrete toxicologic diagnosis.

triage.name: Somatic symptom disorder
triage.reason: Persistent distressing symptoms with disproportionate health-related thoughts and behaviors support diagnosis. Symptoms need not be medically unexplained, and coexisting disease still requires appropriate assessment.

triage.name: Conversion disorder
triage.reason: Functional neurologic symptoms can be diagnosed through positive examination findings showing incompatibility with recognized neurologic disease, with targeted evaluation for alternatives.

triage.name: Illness anxiety disorder
triage.reason: Persistent fear of serious illness despite absent or mild physical symptoms, accompanied by checking or avoidance, supports an interview-based diagnosis after appropriate clinical assessment.

triage.name: Postpartum psychosis
triage.reason: Acute postpartum psychosis, mood changes and disorganization create a psychiatric emergency requiring safety assessment and evaluation for medical causes.

triage.name: Cocaine intoxication
triage.reason: Exposure history and a sympathomimetic presentation support diagnosis, with targeted testing for cardiac, neurologic and metabolic complications.

triage.name: Factitious disorder
triage.reason: A case can establish deliberate falsification or induction of illness without an obvious external reward. Diagnosis requires evidence of deception, not merely unexplained symptoms or inconsistent reports.

triage.name: Body dysmorphic disorder
triage.reason: Preoccupation with perceived appearance defects, repetitive checking or grooming, and functional impairment allow an interview-based diagnosis with assessment of insight and safety.

triage.name: Catatonia
triage.reason: Characteristic motor and behavioral signs support recognition of the syndrome, followed by evaluation for psychiatric, neurologic, medical and medication-related causes.

triage.name: Tardive dyskinesia
triage.reason: Characteristic involuntary movements and a history of dopamine receptor-blocking medication exposure permit diagnosis and distinction from other movement disorders.

triage.name: Acute dystonic reaction
triage.reason: Sudden sustained muscle contractions after a relevant medication exposure create a recognizable clinical case, including assessment for potentially dangerous laryngeal involvement.

triage.name: Cluster headache
triage.reason: Recurrent brief attacks of severe unilateral orbital or temporal pain with ipsilateral autonomic signs and restlessness support a distinctive headache diagnosis.

triage.name: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension
triage.reason: Headache, papilledema and visual symptoms lead to neuroimaging with venous evaluation before lumbar puncture confirms elevated opening pressure with normal CSF composition and exclusion of secondary causes.

triage.name: Vestibular neuritis
triage.reason: Acute persistent vertigo with peripheral vestibular findings and no new hearing loss supports diagnosis after assessing for posterior circulation stroke. Labyrinthitis is distinct and includes auditory involvement.

triage.name: Frontotemporal dementia
triage.reason: Progressive behavioral, executive or language changes, collateral history, cognitive examination and brain imaging support diagnosis and distinction from psychiatric illness and other dementias.

triage.name: Essential tremor
triage.reason: A chronic bilateral upper-limb action tremor, examination for other neurologic signs and review of medication or metabolic causes support a clinical diagnosis.

triage.name: Transverse myelitis
triage.reason: Acute or subacute spinal cord dysfunction with weakness, a sensory level and autonomic symptoms prompts urgent MRI to exclude compression, followed by evaluation for inflammatory and infectious causes.

triage.name: Narcolepsy
triage.reason: Excessive daytime sleepiness, associated sleep phenomena and objective sleep testing support a distinct diagnosis with important mimics.

triage.name: Salicylate poisoning
triage.reason: Exposure history, tinnitus, respiratory findings, acid-base abnormalities and serial salicylate levels create a distinctive toxicology workup.

triage.name: Supraventricular tachycardia
triage.reason: An abrupt episode of palpitations with a regular narrow-complex tachycardia is a practical case diagnosed through history, examination and ECG.

triage.name: Ventricular tachycardia
triage.reason: Palpitations, syncope or hemodynamic compromise lead to ECG diagnosis and urgent distinction from other wide-complex rhythms.

triage.name: Epidural hematoma
triage.reason: Head trauma with evolving neurologic findings prompts urgent head CT, providing a clear diagnosis and important intracranial bleeding differential.

triage.name: Subdural hematoma
triage.reason: Acute neurologic deterioration or delayed headache and cognitive changes can be evaluated through trauma history, neurologic examination and head CT.

triage.name: Cauda equina syndrome
triage.reason: Back pain with urinary dysfunction, saddle sensory changes or leg deficits supports an urgent neurologic examination and lumbar MRI.

triage.name: Organophosphate poisoning
triage.reason: Exposure history and a cholinergic toxidrome provide a recognizable diagnosis requiring immediate clinical assessment without waiting for confirmatory testing.

triage.name: Tricyclic antidepressant poisoning
triage.reason: Medication exposure, anticholinergic findings, altered mental status and ECG conduction abnormalities support a focused emergency toxicology case.

triage.name: Beta-blocker overdose
triage.reason: Medication history, bradycardia, hypotension and ECG findings support diagnosis while requiring evaluation for other causes of shock and drug toxicity.

triage.name: Digoxin toxicity
triage.reason: Medication and renal history, gastrointestinal or neurologic symptoms, arrhythmias and appropriately timed digoxin levels support a specific diagnosis.

triage.name: Acute alcohol intoxication
triage.reason: Recent alcohol use with impaired coordination, speech or consciousness supports diagnosis, while examination and targeted tests assess dangerous alternative causes.

triage.name: Epistaxis
triage.reason: A focused history and nasal examination can establish the bleeding source, assess severity and identify local or systemic contributors.

triage.name: Dental abscess
triage.reason: Focal tooth pain, swelling and oral examination support diagnosis, with imaging when needed to assess the source or deeper spread.

triage.name: Peritonsillar abscess
triage.reason: Unilateral throat pain, trismus and asymmetric oropharyngeal findings form a distinct presentation, with aspiration or imaging when needed.

triage.name: Retropharyngeal abscess
triage.reason: Fever, neck stiffness and swallowing difficulty prompt airway assessment and, when stable, neck imaging to identify a deep neck infection.

triage.name: Snake bite
triage.reason: Exposure history, wound examination and serial assessment for local injury, coagulopathy or neurologic toxicity allow evaluation for envenomation.

triage.name: Ethylene glycol poisoning
triage.reason: Exposure history, altered mental status, metabolic acidosis and evolving kidney injury support a diagnostic workup using toxic alcohol testing and metabolic studies.

triage.name: Skin abscess
triage.reason: A painful, swollen skin lesion can be diagnosed by examination, with ultrasound when needed to distinguish a drainable collection from cellulitis.

triage.name: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
triage.reason: Medication timing, fever, extensive rash, facial edema and laboratory evidence of hematologic or organ involvement support diagnosis and exclusion of mimics.

triage.name: Erythema nodosum
triage.reason: Tender bilateral shin nodules support a clinical diagnosis, with history and targeted testing used to identify triggers such as infection, medications, sarcoidosis, or inflammatory bowel disease.

triage.name: Stasis dermatitis
triage.reason: Pruritic lower-leg eczema, edema, and pigment changes in a patient with venous insufficiency form a recognizable clinical case, with cellulitis and contact dermatitis as important alternatives.

triage.name: Dermatomyositis
triage.reason: Characteristic skin findings and proximal weakness lead to a focused inflammatory myopathy workup, with opportunities to assess swallowing, pulmonary involvement, and associated malignancy risk in adults.

triage.name: Pediculosis capitis
triage.reason: Scalp itching and exposure history prompt scalp and hair examination; finding live lice confirms active infestation and distinguishes it from dandruff and other causes of scalp pruritus.

triage.name: Stable angina
triage.reason: Reproducible exertional chest discomfort supports a focused history, cardiovascular examination and appropriate ischemia testing.

triage.name: Acute pericarditis
triage.reason: Pleuritic, positional chest pain, examination findings and ECG or imaging findings create a distinct diagnostic case with important cardiac alternatives.

triage.name: Acute pancreatitis
triage.reason: Acute epigastric pain, pancreatic enzyme testing and selective imaging allow diagnosis and investigation of common causes.

triage.name: Vasospastic angina
triage.reason: Episodic rest chest pain with transient ischemic ECG changes supports a focused case, with coronary evaluation to distinguish other ischemic causes.

triage.name: Acute myocarditis
triage.reason: Chest pain, arrhythmia or new heart failure can prompt cardiac biomarkers, echocardiography and cardiac MRI to support diagnosis.

triage.name: Uremic encephalopathy
triage.reason: Altered mental status in advanced kidney failure supports a diagnostic case requiring metabolic evaluation and exclusion of other causes of encephalopathy.

triage.name: Cytomegalovirus mononucleosis
triage.reason: A febrile mononucleosis-like illness with atypical lymphocytes can be distinguished from EBV and other infections using targeted testing.

triage.name: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
triage.reason: Visual symptoms in an immunocompromised patient lead to urgent dilated retinal examination with characteristic findings.

triage.name: Cytomegalovirus colitis
triage.reason: Diarrhea, abdominal pain or bleeding in a susceptible patient can be investigated with endoscopy and biopsy to establish tissue-invasive infection.

triage.name: Diabetic macular edema
triage.reason: Central visual blurring in a patient with diabetes can be evaluated by retinal examination and optical coherence tomography.

triage.name: Shigellosis
triage.reason: Acute diarrhea, fever and possible dysentery combine with exposure history and stool testing to yield a specific infectious diagnosis.

triage.name: Microscopic colitis
triage.reason: Chronic watery, nonbloody diarrhea with a usually normal-appearing colon requires colonic biopsies, making a clear diagnostic workup case.

triage.name: Colonic diverticulosis
triage.reason: A specific structural diagnosis demonstrable on colonoscopy or imaging, although usually incidental and less suitable for a symptom-driven case than its complications.

triage.name: Diverticular hemorrhage
triage.reason: Abrupt, usually painless hematochezia supports a lower gastrointestinal bleeding case with stabilization followed by appropriate bleeding-source evaluation.

triage.name: Chronic venous insufficiency
triage.reason: Dependent leg edema, characteristic skin changes and possible venous ulcers support clinical diagnosis and targeted duplex ultrasound.

triage.name: Mallory-Weiss tear
triage.reason: Hematemesis following retching or vomiting provides a focused history, with upper endoscopy identifying the mucosal tear.

triage.name: Esophageal variceal hemorrhage
triage.reason: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding with evidence of portal hypertension requires immediate stabilization and urgent endoscopic diagnosis and treatment.

triage.name: Erosive gastritis
triage.reason: Epigastric symptoms or upper gastrointestinal bleeding, relevant medication and alcohol exposures, and endoscopic erosions support a specific diagnosis.

triage.name: Ischemic colitis
triage.reason: Acute abdominal pain followed by bloody stool, relevant vascular or low-flow risks, and imaging with selective endoscopy create a strong diagnostic case.

triage.name: Colonic angiodysplasia
triage.reason: Painless gastrointestinal bleeding or iron deficiency anemia leads to a differential diagnosis and colonoscopic identification of vascular lesions.

triage.name: Aortic regurgitation
triage.reason: A characteristic diastolic murmur, peripheral findings and possible heart failure symptoms support a diagnosis confirmed and graded by echocardiography.

triage.name: Mitral stenosis
triage.reason: Exertional dyspnea, an apical diastolic murmur and possible atrial fibrillation lead to echocardiographic confirmation.

triage.name: Tricuspid regurgitation
triage.reason: A systolic murmur that increases with inspiration and signs of systemic venous congestion lead to echocardiographic diagnosis and evaluation of the cause.

triage.name: Cryptococcal meningitis
triage.reason: Subacute headache, fever and neurologic symptoms, often with immunosuppression, prompt a safely sequenced lumbar puncture and cryptococcal testing.

triage.name: Functional dyspepsia
triage.reason: Chronic epigastric discomfort, early satiety or postprandial fullness supports a clinical diagnosis after appropriate evaluation excludes explanatory organic disease.

triage.name: Gastritis
triage.reason: Dyspepsia or gastrointestinal bleeding can prompt evaluation of gastric inflammation and its causes; symptoms alone do not establish gastritis, and biopsy can confirm it.

triage.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
triage.reason: Exposure history, cough, dyspnea, crackles and characteristic chest imaging provide an integrated diagnostic case, with additional pulmonary testing when needed.

triage.name: Simple renal cyst
triage.reason: Usually incidental, but a renal lesion found during evaluation can be diagnosed as a simple cyst by characteristic imaging and distinguished from a complex cyst or solid mass.

triage.name: Acquired cystic kidney disease
triage.reason: Advanced chronic kidney disease, often with prolonged dialysis, and multiple renal cysts on imaging allow distinction from inherited cystic disease; hematuria may prompt evaluation.

triage.name: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
triage.reason: Persistent lymphadenopathy, constitutional symptoms or extranodal findings lead to tissue biopsy, which establishes lymphoma and identifies the subtype.

triage.name: Alcohol-induced acute pancreatitis
triage.reason: Acute epigastric pain and elevated pancreatic enzymes establish pancreatitis; alcohol history and assessment for competing causes support the etiology.

triage.name: Chronic pancreatitis
triage.reason: Recurrent or chronic upper abdominal pain, risk factors and possible malabsorption or diabetes lead to pancreatic imaging and assessment of pancreatic function.

triage.name: Cardiogenic shock
triage.reason: Hypoperfusion with evidence of cardiac dysfunction supports an urgent diagnostic case using examination, ECG, bedside echocardiography and laboratory testing alongside stabilization.

triage.name: Schatzki ring
triage.reason: Intermittent solid-food dysphagia or food impaction leads to identification of a distal esophageal ring by endoscopy or barium esophagram.

triage.name: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
triage.reason: A positive urine culture without urinary or attributable systemic symptoms is a diagnosable finding; history distinguishes it from symptomatic infection and guides whether treatment is indicated.

triage.name: Acute tubular necrosis
triage.reason: Acute kidney injury after ischemia or nephrotoxic exposure can be distinguished from prerenal and obstructive causes through history, urine sediment and targeted testing.

triage.name: Postrenal acute kidney injury
triage.reason: Acute kidney injury with retention, obstructive symptoms or relevant risk factors leads to bladder assessment and urinary tract imaging to identify obstruction.

triage.name: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
triage.reason: Proteinuria, edema or declining kidney function leads to a glomerular workup and kidney biopsy, followed by evaluation for primary, secondary or genetic causes.

triage.name: Lupus nephritis
triage.reason: Proteinuria, hematuria or kidney dysfunction with known or suspected lupus leads to urine studies, serologic evaluation and kidney biopsy when indicated.

triage.name: Erosive esophagitis
triage.reason: Reflux symptoms, dysphagia or bleeding prompt evaluation, with endoscopy establishing erosive mucosal injury and distinguishing alternative causes.

triage.name: Inducible laryngeal obstruction
triage.reason: Episodic inspiratory difficulty and trigger patterns suggest the diagnosis; laryngoscopy during symptoms confirms it and helps distinguish asthma.

triage.name: Sulfonamide antibiotic allergy
triage.reason: Medication timing and reaction phenotype support a clinical diagnosis. Risk assessment distinguishes allergy from intolerance and identifies severe reactions; selected low-risk histories may undergo supervised challenge.

triage.name: Small bowel obstruction
triage.reason: Abdominal pain, vomiting, distention and obstipation lead to imaging confirmation, with examination and testing assessing strangulation or ischemia.

triage.name: Inguinal hernia
triage.reason: A groin bulge or discomfort is usually diagnosed by examination, with imaging for uncertain cases and assessment for incarceration or strangulation.

triage.name: Pneumothorax
triage.reason: Acute pleuritic pain and dyspnea prompt examination and chest imaging; suspected tension physiology requires immediate treatment without waiting for imaging.

triage.name: Thoracic aortic aneurysm
triage.reason: Often found incidentally, but risk factors, compressive symptoms or aortic regurgitation can prompt diagnostic imaging. Acute pain requires evaluation for dissection or rupture.

triage.name: Femoral hernia
triage.reason: A groin mass below the inguinal ligament or bowel obstruction supports a focused examination and imaging workup, with particular concern for strangulation.

triage.name: Incisional hernia
triage.reason: A bulge at a prior surgical incision is evaluated through surgical history and examination, with imaging when needed and assessment for obstructive complications.

triage.name: Epigastric hernia
triage.reason: A focal midline bulge or tenderness above the umbilicus can be diagnosed by examination, with ultrasound when the finding is uncertain.

triage.name: Postoperative ileus
triage.reason: Postoperative distention, nausea and delayed bowel function require review of medications, electrolytes and imaging when indicated to exclude mechanical obstruction or other complications.

triage.name: Bacterial meningitis
triage.reason: Fever, headache, meningeal signs or altered mental status prompt urgent cultures and lumbar puncture when safe, without delaying empiric antibiotics for imaging or procedural delays.

triage.name: Tinea capitis
triage.reason: Scalp scale, broken hairs and patchy alopecia provide recognizable findings, with fungal microscopy or culture supporting diagnosis and distinguishing other causes of hair loss.

triage.name: Childhood absence epilepsy
triage.reason: Brief, frequent staring spells with abrupt recovery are characterized through caregiver history and EEG, distinguishing seizures from inattention and other seizure types.

triage.name: Laryngomalacia
triage.reason: Infant inspiratory stridor with characteristic positional and feeding associations leads to flexible laryngoscopy, while growth and respiratory status establish severity.

triage.name: Adenotonsillar hypertrophy
triage.reason: Snoring, mouth breathing and nasal obstruction prompt examination and assessment of adenoidal enlargement, with sleep testing when indicated for suspected obstructive sleep apnea.

triage.name: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
triage.reason: Growth records, pubertal examination, family history and delayed bone age support the diagnosis after appropriate exclusion of chronic disease and endocrine causes.

triage.name: Gestational diabetes
triage.reason: Usually asymptomatic, it is reached through prenatal history and appropriately timed glucose screening and diagnostic testing, distinguishing it from overt preexisting diabetes.

triage.name: Lactational mastitis
triage.reason: Breast pain, focal erythema and systemic symptoms during lactation support a clinical diagnosis; persistent or focal findings may require ultrasound to assess for abscess.

triage.name: Tubal factor infertility
triage.reason: An infertility history and risk factors guide a couple-based evaluation, with tubal patency testing identifying obstruction and distinguishing other causes of infertility.

triage.name: Hyperprolactinemia
triage.reason: Amenorrhea, galactorrhea or hypogonadal symptoms lead to prolactin testing and evaluation for pregnancy, medications, hypothyroidism and pituitary disease.

triage.name: Unexplained infertility
triage.reason: A diagnosis of exclusion after an appropriate infertility evaluation shows ovulation, tubal patency and no significant semen abnormality.

triage.name: Gestational hypertension
triage.reason: New hypertension after 20 weeks is diagnosed through repeated blood pressure measurements and evaluation excluding preeclampsia and preexisting hypertension.

triage.name: Chronic hypertension in pregnancy
triage.reason: History and blood pressure measurements establish hypertension predating pregnancy or detected before 20 weeks; evaluation assesses baseline organ function and superimposed preeclampsia when indicated.

triage.name: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
triage.reason: Usually asymptomatic, but abnormal cervical screening provides a realistic presentation leading to risk-based colposcopy and biopsy confirmation of a precancerous lesion.

triage.name: Anencephaly
triage.reason: A prenatal diagnostic case in which abnormal screening or routine ultrasound leads to identification of absent cranial vault and major cerebral structures.

triage.name: Follicular ovarian cyst
triage.reason: Pelvic discomfort or an incidental adnexal finding prompts pregnancy testing and ultrasound, with morphology and clinical course supporting a functional follicular cyst.

triage.name: Corpus luteum cyst
triage.reason: Pelvic pain or an incidental ovarian lesion can be evaluated with pregnancy testing and ultrasound, while excluding ectopic pregnancy and torsion when clinically indicated.

triage.name: Hemorrhagic ovarian cyst
triage.reason: Acute unilateral pelvic pain supports a focused workup with pregnancy testing and pelvic ultrasound, distinguishing hemorrhagic cyst from ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion.

triage.name: Stress urinary incontinence
triage.reason: Leakage with coughing or exertion is characterized by history, pelvic examination and a cough stress test, with urinalysis helping exclude infection.

triage.name: Mixed urinary incontinence
triage.reason: History identifies both urgency-associated leakage and leakage with exertion; examination and basic urinary evaluation distinguish it from infection, retention and isolated incontinence subtypes.

triage.name: Endometrial polyp
triage.reason: Intermenstrual or postmenopausal bleeding prompts evaluation with ultrasound and, when needed, saline infusion sonography or hysteroscopy, with tissue assessment to exclude malignancy.

triage.name: Cervical polyp
triage.reason: Postcoital or intermenstrual bleeding can lead to identification of a cervical polyp on speculum examination, with histologic evaluation after removal.

triage.name: Adenomyosis
triage.reason: Heavy menstrual bleeding, dysmenorrhea and a globular enlarged uterus support a clinical diagnosis, with transvaginal ultrasound or selected MRI helping distinguish fibroids and other causes.

triage.name: Endometrial hyperplasia
triage.reason: Abnormal uterine bleeding and risk factors for unopposed estrogen lead to indicated endometrial sampling, which establishes hyperplasia and determines whether atypia is present.

triage.name: Abnormal uterine bleeding due to ovulatory dysfunction
triage.reason: Irregular, unpredictable bleeding is evaluated through menstrual history, pregnancy testing and targeted investigation for endocrine, structural and endometrial causes.

triage.name: Atrophic vaginitis
triage.reason: Vaginal dryness, burning and dyspareunia in a hypoestrogenic patient are assessed through history and pelvic examination, with testing when needed to exclude infection.

triage.name: Müllerian agenesis
triage.reason: Primary amenorrhea with normal breast development leads to examination and pelvic imaging showing absent or underdeveloped Müllerian structures, with testing to distinguish androgen insensitivity.

triage.name: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome
triage.reason: Primary amenorrhea with breast development, sparse pubic hair and an absent uterus prompts hormone testing and chromosome analysis to establish the diagnosis.

triage.name: Imperforate hymen
triage.reason: Primary amenorrhea with cyclic pelvic pain, sometimes urinary retention, leads to external genital examination and ultrasound demonstrating outflow obstruction and hematocolpos.

triage.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
triage.reason: Persistent excessive worry, associated symptoms, functional impairment and exclusion of medical or substance-related causes support a clear diagnostic interview.

triage.name: Anorexia nervosa
triage.reason: Restriction, significantly low weight and weight-related fears or behaviors create a diagnostic case requiring assessment of medical instability and alternative causes of weight loss.

triage.name: Bulimia nervosa
triage.reason: Recurrent binge eating and compensatory behaviors can be established through interview, with examination and testing for complications and competing diagnoses.

triage.name: Separation anxiety disorder
triage.reason: Developmentally inappropriate separation fears, avoidance and impairment provide a recognizable interview-based diagnosis distinct from normal childhood anxiety.

triage.name: Cocaine use disorder
triage.reason: A history of impaired control and continued cocaine use despite harm supports diagnosis; toxicology can support exposure but does not establish the disorder.

triage.name: Cocaine withdrawal
triage.reason: Dysphoria, fatigue, sleep changes and craving after cessation of sustained cocaine use form a clinical syndrome requiring assessment for suicidality and other causes.

triage.name: Benzodiazepine withdrawal
triage.reason: Anxiety, insomnia, tremor and autonomic symptoms after dose reduction or cessation support diagnosis; seizures and delirium make recognition clinically important.

triage.name: Avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder
triage.reason: Restricted intake with nutritional or psychosocial consequences, without weight-shape concerns driving restriction, supports a case requiring medical and feeding-history assessment.

triage.name: Specific phobia
triage.reason: Persistent, disproportionate fear of a specific object or situation, avoidance and functional impairment can be established through a focused clinical interview.

triage.name: Agoraphobia
triage.reason: Fear and avoidance of situations where escape or help may be difficult provide a distinct interview-based diagnosis, separable from panic disorder and social anxiety.

triage.name: Costochondritis
triage.reason: Localized chest wall pain and reproducible costochondral tenderness support diagnosis after history and risk-based evaluation for dangerous causes of chest pain.

triage.name: Acute otitis externa
triage.reason: Ear pain, tragal or pinna tenderness and an inflamed ear canal provide a clear examination-based diagnosis with important middle-ear and invasive infection alternatives.

triage.name: Staphylococcal food poisoning
triage.reason: Abrupt vomiting shortly after a shared food exposure supports a presumptive toxin-mediated diagnosis; routine individual cases generally do not require confirmatory testing.

triage.name: Bacillus cereus food poisoning
triage.reason: Food exposure, incubation and vomiting-predominant or diarrheal symptoms support a presumptive diagnosis, though clinical overlap with other foodborne illnesses limits certainty.

triage.name: Clostridium perfringens food poisoning
triage.reason: Abdominal cramps and diarrhea after a compatible shared meal support a presumptive diagnosis; outbreak testing can distinguish it from similar foodborne illnesses.

triage.name: Herpetic whitlow
triage.reason: Painful grouped finger vesicles and exposure history support diagnosis, with lesion PCR when needed; distinguishing it from a bacterial felon prevents inappropriate drainage.

triage.name: Viral conjunctivitis
triage.reason: Watery discharge, conjunctival injection and exposure or respiratory symptoms support diagnosis, while examination screens for corneal disease and other dangerous red-eye causes.

triage.name: Acute viral pharyngitis
triage.reason: Sore throat with compatible viral symptoms and examination findings supports diagnosis; streptococcal testing is reserved for presentations where it is indicated.

triage.name: Functional urinary incontinence
triage.reason: Urine leakage related to mobility, cognitive or environmental barriers can be identified through history and functional assessment while evaluating other urinary causes.

triage.name: Acute cystitis
triage.reason: Acute dysuria, frequency and urgency provide a classic diagnostic case, using urinalysis and selective culture while distinguishing pyelonephritis, urethritis and vaginitis.

triage.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
triage.reason: An acute headache or altered mental status presentation requiring urgent neurologic assessment and appropriately sequenced imaging and further testing.

triage.name: Tension-type headache
triage.reason: A common clinical diagnosis reached through headache history, a normal neurologic examination, and assessment for secondary headache warning signs.

triage.name: Diabetic neuropathy
triage.reason: Typical distal sensory symptoms and examination findings in a patient with diabetes support diagnosis while prompting evaluation for alternative neuropathy causes.

triage.name: Meningioma
triage.reason: Progressive focal deficits, seizures, or headaches can lead to characteristic neuroimaging findings. Most meningiomas are benign rather than malignant.

triage.name: Brain metastases
triage.reason: New seizures, focal deficits, or progressive headaches can prompt brain imaging and evaluation for a known or previously unrecognized primary malignancy.

triage.name: Vascular dementia
triage.reason: Cognitive and functional decline, vascular history, neurologic examination, cognitive testing, and imaging allow differentiation from other causes of dementia.

triage.name: Vestibular migraine
triage.reason: Recurrent vestibular episodes with migraine history and associated features support a clinical diagnosis after considering peripheral vestibular and central causes.

triage.name: Medication-overuse headache
triage.reason: Frequent headaches and a detailed history of acute headache medication use establish a recognizable secondary headache diagnosis.

triage.name: Obstructive hydrocephalus
triage.reason: Symptoms and signs of raised intracranial pressure lead to imaging that identifies ventricular enlargement and obstruction, requiring urgent neurosurgical assessment.

triage.name: Communicating hydrocephalus
triage.reason: A coherent diagnosis based on neurologic symptoms and ventricular enlargement without an intraventricular obstruction; history helps identify hemorrhagic, infectious, or other causes.

triage.name: Focal epilepsy
triage.reason: Recurrent stereotyped focal events, witness history, EEG, and brain imaging support diagnosis and distinguish epilepsy from syncope and other episodic disorders.

triage.name: Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy
triage.reason: Adolescent-onset morning myoclonic jerks, often with generalized seizures, provide a characteristic history that can be supported by EEG.

triage.name: Diffuse axonal injury
triage.reason: Severe impaired consciousness after acceleration-deceleration trauma, sometimes disproportionate to initial CT findings, supports a diagnostic case with collateral history and MRI.

triage.name: Enhanced physiologic tremor
triage.reason: A fine postural or action tremor with identifiable triggers can be diagnosed through history, examination, and targeted evaluation for medication or metabolic contributors.

triage.name: Drug-induced tremor
triage.reason: Medication timing, dose changes, tremor characterization, and exclusion of other causes make this a useful adverse drug effect case.

triage.name: Heat stroke
triage.reason: Heat exposure or exertion with hyperthermia and central nervous system dysfunction creates a clear emergency diagnosis requiring immediate cooling without waiting for laboratory results.

triage.name: Cardiac tamponade
triage.reason: Dyspnea or shock with suggestive cardiovascular findings and urgent echocardiography supports a high-value diagnosis requiring rapid intervention.

triage.name: Dog bite
triage.reason: Exposure history and wound examination establish the injury, with assessment for deep structural damage, infection, tetanus protection, and rabies risk.

triage.name: Benzodiazepine poisoning
triage.reason: Sedation, ataxia, and exposure history support diagnosis while requiring assessment of airway safety, co-ingestants, and alternative causes of depressed consciousness.

triage.name: Methamphetamine intoxication
triage.reason: Agitation, autonomic activation, and stimulant exposure support a clinical toxidrome diagnosis, with evaluation for hyperthermia, cardiovascular complications, and other causes.

triage.name: Corneal foreign body
triage.reason: Acute foreign-body sensation, tearing and exposure history lead to diagnosis by careful ocular examination and fluorescein staining.

triage.name: Traumatic hyphema
triage.reason: Blunt ocular trauma followed by pain or blurred vision supports a focused examination identifying blood in the anterior chamber.

triage.name: Open globe injury
triage.reason: An important ocular emergency recognized from injury mechanism, visual loss and cautious examination, with imaging when needed and avoidance of pressure on the globe.

triage.name: Orbital floor fracture
triage.reason: Facial trauma with diplopia, impaired eye movement or infraorbital numbness creates a focused case confirmed by orbital CT.

triage.name: Skull fracture
triage.reason: Head trauma, characteristic examination findings and CT allow a specific diagnosis while assessing associated intracranial injury.

triage.name: Cerebral contusion
triage.reason: Trauma history, altered mental status or focal deficits and head CT support diagnosis and distinction from other traumatic intracranial lesions.

triage.name: Traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage
triage.reason: Head trauma followed by headache or neurologic changes prompts noncontrast head CT, which identifies subarachnoid bleeding.

triage.name: Herpes simplex keratitis
triage.reason: A painful, photophobic red eye with characteristic corneal findings on fluorescein and slit-lamp examination provides a distinctive diagnostic case.

triage.name: Smoke inhalation injury
triage.reason: Fire exposure, airway and respiratory findings, and targeted testing support diagnosis while evaluating associated carbon monoxide or cyanide toxicity.

triage.name: Benzodiazepine intoxication
triage.reason: Exposure history, sedation and ataxia support a clinical diagnosis while glucose testing and evaluation for coingestants address dangerous alternatives.

triage.name: Hypovolemic shock
triage.reason: A recognizable clinical syndrome reached through evidence of hypoperfusion and volume loss, with focused testing to identify hemorrhage or nonhemorrhagic losses.

triage.name: Obstructive shock
triage.reason: A diagnosable shock mechanism using examination and bedside imaging; a useful case should establish the specific obstructing cause rather than stop at the syndrome.

triage.name: Neurogenic shock
triage.reason: Hypotension with relative bradycardia after cervical or high thoracic spinal cord injury supports diagnosis after actively evaluating hemorrhage and other causes of shock.

triage.name: ACE inhibitor-induced angioedema
triage.reason: Medication history and characteristic swelling, usually without urticaria, support a clinical diagnosis requiring immediate assessment for airway involvement.

triage.name: Laryngospasm
triage.reason: Sudden upper-airway obstruction in a compatible setting is clinically recognizable and distinguishable from bronchospasm, foreign-body obstruction and laryngeal edema.

triage.name: Seborrheic dermatitis
triage.reason: Characteristic scaling and distribution on the scalp, face or other sebaceous areas allow clinical diagnosis and comparison with psoriasis and fungal infection.

triage.name: Tinea corporis
triage.reason: An expanding scaly annular eruption supports a focused skin case, with potassium hydroxide microscopy when confirmation is needed.

triage.name: Alopecia areata
triage.reason: Well-demarcated nonscarring hair loss and characteristic examination findings support diagnosis while distinguishing tinea capitis and traumatic hair loss.

triage.name: Tinea cruris
triage.reason: A pruritic groin eruption with a scaly advancing border offers a focused diagnostic case, supported when needed by potassium hydroxide microscopy.

triage.name: Tinea unguium
triage.reason: Thickened, discolored nails prompt examination and fungal confirmation to distinguish dermatophyte infection from psoriasis, trauma and other nail disorders.

triage.name: Cutaneous small-vessel vasculitis
triage.reason: Palpable purpura supports a focused skin examination, medication and infection history, skin biopsy, and evaluation for systemic involvement and mimics.

triage.name: Fixed drug eruption
triage.reason: A sharply demarcated lesion recurring at the same site after medication exposure provides a recognizable diagnosis through history and skin examination.

triage.name: Diabetic retinopathy
triage.reason: Diabetes history and characteristic findings on dilated retinal examination establish the diagnosis; visual symptoms and retinal imaging can support a case and distinguish complications.

triage.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
triage.reason: Brief episodes of position-triggered vertigo and characteristic positional nystagmus allow bedside diagnosis while testing students' ability to recognize central causes of dizziness.
